papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer predictive behavior from large, expensive models to smaller, faster models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade research has produced a taxonomy of distillation mechanisms (logit/soft-target matching, representation or feature imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers), adaptations for low-data or data-free settings, and combinations of distillation with architecture search and pruning. Empirical work shows that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance at large computational savings, but also highlights practical failure modes: students often do not perfectly match teacher predictive distributions, optimization choices and training data matter strongly, and specialized methods are needed for task-specific or distributed scenarios. Recent advances emphasize multi-stage/multi-teacher schedules, augmentation-aware objectives, online distributed training, and loss formulations that better capture teacher uncertainty; combining these approaches with automated architecture search and structured pruning yields stronger, hardware-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a multifaceted set of techniques for creating smaller, faster models from large neural teachers. Methods span soft-output transfer, intermediate-representation and attention matching, relational/contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-centric strategies including synthetic or data-free approaches. KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows strong practical gains across NLP and other modalities, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher and student, data strategies, and attention to robustness and domain-shift limitations.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted training paradigm that enables compact, deployable models by transferring aspects of teacher models to smaller students. When treated as a central tool rather than a single recipe, KD supports a range of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), deployment modalities (on-device, federated, data-limited), and complementary compressions (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to adapt data and curricula; with these considerations KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though optimization subtleties and robustness remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single training trick but a central, practical framework for compressing large models into deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-label transfer, representation-level alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and integration with other compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate design: choosing which teacher signals to transfer, addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, and using data-aware or data-free strategies when original training data are unavailable. I argue that KD should be the core component of any production-focused compression pipeline, paired with representation-level objectives and careful data strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile suite of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment of distilled models depends on matching the distillation recipe to task constraints (data availability, teacher–student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and privacy or communication limits) and frequently benefits from multi-stage or task-aware distillation schedules. While KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance, open issues remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable methods for distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile, practically oriented set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure, and is most effective when combined with complementary practices such as pre-training compact students, careful selection or synthesis of distillation data, teacher scheduling, and architecture-aware alignment. Empirical work shows KD routinely enables meaningful latency and memory reductions with modest accuracy loss, but success depends on principled design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; these considerations motivate task-aware pipelines and ongoing research into robustness, fairness, privacy, and theoretical underpinnings.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Nuanced Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for creating compact, deployable models from large teachers. When treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables significant reductions in memory, compute, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Its success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage data (real, augmented, or synthesized), and how KD is integrated with complementary compression methods. KD is powerful for production constraints but must be applied with task-aware design to avoid propagating teacher weaknesses or failing under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Integrations, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible pathway to convert large, high-performing deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture-aware surgery to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its empirical strengths include preserving much of teacher performance while enabling large efficiency gains; its limitations arise from teacher–student mismatch, data availability constraints, possible propagation of teacher defects, and robustness or fairness trade-offs. Effective deployment treats KD as the core of a hybrid compression toolkit and requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacities, how to handle scarce or private data, and when to combine KD with low-precision numerics or structured pruning.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques shrink large neural models into smaller, faster models for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. A diverse set of approaches—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or generative sample synthesis—has emerged across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention maps, or structural priors), how to align heterogeneous architectures, whether teacher or student are adapted during training, and how to handle limited or absent training data. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost are possible with modest performance loss, but open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robustness under domain shift, privacy, and closing optimization/capacity gaps between teachers and students.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for transferring capabilities from large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or modality-limited models. When combined with complementary strategies—domain adaptation, feature-level matching, data augmentation, and meta-learning—distillation enables practical deployment across constrained devices, heterogeneous federated systems, and domain-shifted settings. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization subtleties and mismatches between teacher and student require methodological care and, in some cases, alternative regularization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature imitation, relational/attention transfer, and progressive module replacement—and is used together with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical evidence shows that, when designed for the teacher/student pair and deployment constraints, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What is Known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Existing practice spans matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or attention, online and ensemble distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches when original training data are unavailable. KD is typically combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and shaped by practical concerns—teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how to transfer, data availability or privacy, and robustness—which determine real-world effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for translating large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. Treated as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD combines soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, relational or contrastive objectives, and data-side interventions to produce compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires matching distillation objectives to student capacity and task requirements and combining KD with complementary compression techniques and careful data strategies. Despite its practicality, KD has limits—data scarcity or privacy, capacity mismatch, teacher errors, and robustness under distributional shift—that must be managed through design choices and complementary methods.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple logit-based supervision to richer representation-, relation-, and adversarial-level transfers and is used to enable on-device inference, multi-task models, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and data-limited deployments. Best outcomes arise when KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), task-aware design, careful sample or synthetic-data strategies, and interventions for bias and privacy. KD has clear empirical benefits across modalities but also well-documented limits—sensitivity to data availability and heterogeneity, potential propagation of teacher errors or biases, and the need for architectural and optimization care—motivating principled adaptations and further study.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescriptive Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a central toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware or data-free strategies, and integration with other compression primitives—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of rare behaviors; realizing reliable compressed models requires deliberate teacher preparation, student-aware design, data or synthesis strategies, and explicit robustness and bias interventions.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Methods span data-dependent distillation using teacher soft targets and intermediate hints, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, many-to-many layer mapping for large pre-trained language models, data-free or zero-shot distillation where training data are unavailable, and approaches that combine distillation with quantization or pruning for deployment. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can recover much of a teacher's accuracy while enabling efficiency gains, but trade-offs remain around robustness, optimization difficulty, domain shifts, and the need for careful alignment of inputs or representations. Recent work addresses these challenges with generative replay, adversarial objectives, layer-matching distances, and teacher-annealing strategies, yet open problems include theory of optimization, scalable privacy-preserving protocols, and balancing fairness or robustness with compression.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD works at multiple levels — soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behaviour — and is most effective when combined with data strategies, teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression such as pruning or quantization. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can regularize student training, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align capacities, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; careful, task-aware protocols are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logits matching, distillation can be adapted to transfer inductive biases, deploy in federated or privacy-constrained settings, operate without access to original training data, and improve robustness and domain specialization. When combined with techniques such as feature mimicking, careful soft-label regularization, and online or ensemble-based training regimes, distillation provides a flexible toolkit to meet the efficiency, privacy, and deployment constraints of modern deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teachers to a smaller student model. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to rich objectives that align intermediate representations, exploit multiple teachers, search for task-specific student architectures, and generate or synthesize data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, speech, vision, graphs) and combined with other compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and recurring challenges — data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and principled objective design — and suggests strategies to mitigate them in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Evolving Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. It enables compact, efficient student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, supports deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. Recent advances extend distillation beyond simple logits matching to many-to-many layer mapping, task-adaptive compression, teacher-aware training, adversarial and data-free scenarios, and robustness-aware objectives. Together these developments show that distillation is both a practical engineering tool and a rich research paradigm for addressing capacity, data availability, privacy, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Nuanced Path to Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques to transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary strategies — such as pre-training compact architectures, data augmentation, selective sample transfer, and module-level compression — KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what is transferred, the availability and nature of data, teacher–student design, and optimization choices. Responsible deployment requires understanding both the practical strengths (efficiency, adaptability, applicability to privacy settings) and the limitations (data dependence, optimization gaps, possible degradation on rare or shifted inputs) of distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the core of a hybrid, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Conditional Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and mature training paradigm that enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving—sometimes improving—task performance. As a practical tool, KD spans logits matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free and zero-shot schemes, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Its success in deployment hinges on matching distillation recipes to data availability, model capacity, and application constraints; when so matched, KD enables deployable students that recover much of teacher behavior, but predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, teacher errors, privacy and fairness concerns) require complementary methods and careful protocol design.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical path to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. A range of KD mechanisms—including soft-target supervision, intermediate feature or attention matching, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and input-side augmentation—enable tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, privacy, and robustness. KD works best when its components are selected and adapted to deployment constraints: student capacity, available (or private) data, domain shift, and adversarial threats. However, important limitations remain, including distributional mismatch between teacher and student inputs, the preservation of robustness and fairness properties, and principled teacher selection. This article argues that a hybrid, constraint-aware KD strategy that combines representation-level transfer, data augmentation, and robustness- or privacy-aware synthesis offers the most reliable route to practical compression in real-world NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond matching final outputs, modern KD variants transfer intermediate representations, adapt teacher behavior to students, and operate when task data are limited or unavailable. KD is most effective when combined with task-aware signal selection, teacher design, data strategies, and complementary compression such as architecture search or pruning; used in this way, KD enables compact models that approach teacher performance while addressing real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature imitation, relational/attention transfer, and progressive module replacement—and is used together with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical evidence shows that, when designed for the teacher/student pair and deployment constraints, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students. A rich family of KD methods—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, data-free and data-augmented distillation, and teacher-student co-design—has been developed to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) across vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation objectives, data strategies, and architecture choices are well matched. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, scarcity or absence of real data, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models. Practical pipelines combine pretraining of compact architectures, multi-objective distillation (outputs + internals), data augmentation or synthesis, and teacher adaptation to produce robust, efficient student models.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster models while preserving— and in some settings improving—accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. KD can be adapted to resource-constrained deployment, domain adaptation, privacy- or data-limited settings, and to improve adversarial robustness when paired with targeted techniques. Combining KD with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, structured sparsity, layer mapping) yields practical, high-quality compressed models across modalities including vision, language, graphs, and generative models.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. When treated as a system—deciding what signals to transfer (soft outputs, internal representations, relations), how to prepare or synthesize data, how to design teachers and students, and how to combine KD with complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization—KD enables deployable models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on capacity matching, data availability, and task-aware objectives; addressing robustness, fairness, and privacy requires targeted interventions and monitoring.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of teacher behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit has been developed—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher schedules, data-free or privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows that carefully designed KD pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while delivering substantial latency and memory savings, but success depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and combining KD with complementary compression and training practices. Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, faithful transfer of rare or long-tail behaviors, automated teacher selection, and reliable operation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across computer vision, language, graph, and healthcare applications, KD variants augment or replace naive logit matching with feature/hint matching, data augmentation, layer mapping strategies, and data-free or privacy-aware mechanisms. Practical work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment for pre-trained transformers, and the use of synthetic or mixed inputs to improve student generalization. At the same time, theoretical and empirical studies highlight limitations under data heterogeneity and imperfect teachers, motivating hybrid losses that mix soft and hard labels and methods that control privacy leakage during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Nuanced Path to Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques to transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary strategies — such as pre-training compact architectures, data augmentation, selective sample transfer, and module-level compression — KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what is transferred, the availability and nature of data, teacher–student design, and optimization choices. Responsible deployment requires understanding both the practical strengths (efficiency, adaptability, applicability to privacy settings) and the limitations (data dependence, optimization gaps, possible degradation on rare or shifted inputs) of distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). Across vision and language, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architectural design, and quantization) and with strategies for scarce or missing data to obtain deployable models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and mechanisms to preserve robustness and rare-token behaviors. Data-free distillation, multi-task or multi-teacher schemes, and targeted representation matching extend KD’s applicability to many real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can retain much of the performance of their teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to include feature- and layer-level supervision, online and multi-teacher schemes, meta-learned teachers, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest performance loss, but success depends on careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Remaining practical issues include teacher–student heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, robustness to domain shifts, and limits to compression for some generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Methods span data-dependent distillation using teacher soft targets and intermediate hints, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, many-to-many layer mapping for large pre-trained language models, data-free or zero-shot distillation where training data are unavailable, and approaches that combine distillation with quantization or pruning for deployment. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can recover much of a teacher's accuracy while enabling efficiency gains, but trade-offs remain around robustness, optimization difficulty, domain shifts, and the need for careful alignment of inputs or representations. Recent work addresses these challenges with generative replay, adversarial objectives, layer-matching distances, and teacher-annealing strategies, yet open problems include theory of optimization, scalable privacy-preserving protocols, and balancing fairness or robustness with compression.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. A wide variety of KD strategies—matching softened logits, aligning features or attention maps, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or task-aware augmentation—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on what is distilled, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and provenance of data, and task-specific constraints (e.g., robustness or federated heterogeneity). Carefully designed pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost, but KD also has important failure modes that motivate complementary techniques and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but it is not a single recipe: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, how distillation data are chosen or synthesized, and how complementary compression techniques are applied. Treating KD as a configurable system—combining appropriate loss forms, layer mappings, data strategies, and robustness/privacy safeguards—yields the best trade-offs between compactness and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research has broadened KD from simple softened-logit matching to a toolbox that includes intermediate-feature alignment, relational or attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and staged training schedules, and data strategies ranging from augmentation to synthetic or data-free generation. When combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware adaptation, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Success hinges on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; remaining challenges include domain shift, capacity mismatch, low-frequency behavior in sequence tasks, and privacy-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible engineering paradigm for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what teacher signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data- or curriculum-driven strategies to use—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's task performance. Effective deployment requires pairing distillation with complementary compression methods, pretraining or adaptation of compact architectures, and explicit attention to limits such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, and generative tasks. KD methods extend beyond simple output (logit) matching to include intermediate-representation and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, curriculum and data-aware schedules, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and tuned for teacher–student compatibility and data constraints, KD frequently produces compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Nonetheless, challenges remain in handling capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of rare or tail behaviors, teacher errors and biases, and reliably distilling without access to original data—areas that motivate ongoing research in curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. It has evolved from straightforward soft-label training to richer objectives that match features, attention, or module behaviors, and to deployment-aware variants that address privacy, data scarcity, and heterogeneous devices. Empirical work across vision and language shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation signals, data, and architecture choices are carefully matched; important open problems include data heterogeneity, capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and theoretical understanding of what is actually transferred.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated not as a narrow compression trick but as a unifying, practical paradigm for producing compact, deployable models while preserving accuracy, robustness, and task-specific behavior. KD’s range—spanning soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and adversarial or curriculum-enhanced transfers—makes it uniquely suited to combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. At the same time, KD requires careful design to handle teacher-student mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and data-availability or privacy limits; following representation-aware objectives, adaptive teacher strategies, and hybrid compression pipelines yields the most reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods compress large deep models into smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature shows a spectrum of KD signals (soft logits, intermediate features, layer mappings), enhancements via data interventions and architecture search, and combinations with pruning or low-precision inference. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, what augmentations or synthetic data to use) as well as attention to privacy and robustness. The field has produced effective recipes for compressing pretrained language models, vision transformers, and generative models, while ongoing work clarifies limits and complementary techniques for reliable deployment.
