papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core and Its Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer information at multiple levels (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), be applied with or without original training data, and be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, the availability and nature of data, and how to handle heterogeneity or robustness concerns. A pragmatic KD protocol blends pre-training of compact architectures, appropriate choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free methods when needed), and complementary compression techniques, while actively addressing teacher weighting and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a mere optimization trick but a central, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a system composed of complementary ingredients—teacher design (single, ensemble or multi-teacher), what to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, relational information), how to obtain data (real, synthesized, or data-free), and deployment constraints (privacy, federated or on-device latency)—KD consistently enables strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance across vision, language, generative, and real-world production tasks. Realizing KD’s full potential requires representation- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive teacher–student mappings, careful handling of data scarcity or privacy, and integration with pretraining and other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but it is not a single recipe: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, how distillation data are chosen or synthesized, and how complementary compression techniques are applied. Treating KD as a configurable system—combining appropriate loss forms, layer mappings, data strategies, and robustness/privacy safeguards—yields the best trade-offs between compactness and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of practical and theoretical approaches for shrinking deep models while retaining performance. Methods span logits-based soft-label transfer, layer- and feature-level matching, architecture-aware transformations, teacher improvement or selection strategies, data-free and privacy-preserving pipelines, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Across vision, language, multimodal, and domain-transfer applications, recent work shows that careful design choices—such as how layers are matched, which features to transfer, whether the teacher is static or trained to teach, and how to handle limited or private data—substantially affect the student’s final accuracy and deployment efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Vaughan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Empirical work across vision and NLP shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective distillation is typically a system-level design problem that combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student, how to prepare or synthesize data, and which complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to apply. Practical success hinges on handling capacity mismatch, data availability, distribution shift, and transferred biases; hybrid pipelines that adapt signals and data to the student and task deliver the most reliable trade-offs between compactness and performance.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Adaptive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. KD's successes across vision, speech, and NLP show that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), how to align teacher and student, and whether to rely on original data or generated/synthetic data determines outcomes. To be effective in real deployments, KD must be combined with complementary methods (data-free generation, federated protocols, targeted augmentation, and robustness-aware objectives) and applied adaptively to task and resource constraints. When used thoughtfully, KD enables substantial efficiency gains without wholesale architectural redesign; when used naively it can propagate teacher errors or exacerbate distributional and low-frequency lexical problems.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while often preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. KD methods range from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable; they have been successfully applied across vision, generative modeling, recommender systems, and large pretrained language models. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to address limited or private data, robustness, and bias—so practitioners must pair KD with task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to get reliable, deployable results.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behavior — and by combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, and architecture search — KD enables substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of a teacher’s performance. However, its effectiveness depends on design choices: what signals are distilled, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Treating KD as a configurable, system-level toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the most reliable path to compact, high-quality models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Constraints, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models retain much of the utility of high-capacity systems. KD operates across levels of abstraction (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure) and is routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (quantization, pruning, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation, or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many settings, but success is context-dependent: it depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, or robustness. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, practical variants, and actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured relational signals—and is effective across modalities when paired with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and student-aware architecture design. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, selecting appropriate distillation targets, preparing or synthesizing suitable training data, and validating robustness and fairness. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a system of interacting components (signal selection, data, initialization, and optimization) and couples distillation with architecture-aware transforms, pruning, or quantization to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened teacher logits to a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Modern KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relations), operate in varied data regimes (full-data, few-shot, data-free/zero-shot), and are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device and low-latency deployments when practitioner choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression are task- and capacity-aware. However, KD is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, limited or private data, and distribution shift create failure modes that require careful objective design, student pretraining, and evaluation under deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression across Modalities and Deployment Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from a teacher to a student, KD can preserve accuracy while reducing model size and inference cost. Combining KD with task-aware objectives, data-augmentation strategies, and data-free synthesis techniques further extends its applicability to settings with limited task data, privacy constraints, or strict latency requirements. This paper argues that a principled, hybrid KD approach—tailored to the modality and deployment constraints—offers the best path to deployable, high-quality compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable means to compress large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. When matched to task constraints—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, how to align layers or features, and whether or how to handle missing or private training data—KD enables deployment of competitive models in latency- and resource-constrained settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: careful design (task-aware layer selection, many-to-many mapping for large pre-trained transformers, selective sample weighting, and data-free procedures when needed) is required to avoid propagating teacher errors, worsening robustness, or underfitting compact students. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, but that success depends on matching KD mechanisms to application constraints and combining KD with complementary engineering (efficient distillation pipelines and synthetic-data or adversarial generators when data are unavailable).

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, flexible strategy for compressing and adapting deep models for real-world deployment. When framed as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, teacher ensembles, data-aware synthesis, and architecture-aware compression—KD routinely yields compact students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to address robustness and rare-event behavior; when these are handled explicitly, KD enables reliable, deployable models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention patterns—and often yields substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability relative to naive student training. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and privacy constraints, and whether complementary compression methods are applied. Viewed as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables flexible, task-aware compression pipelines that can be adapted to real-world constraints while acknowledging remaining limits around robustness, data-free operation, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power and internal knowledge from large, expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students), enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, designing many-to-many layer mappings, performing data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable, and distilling ensembles or multiple teachers into a single model. In NLP, these methods are applied to compress pre-trained language models, speed up evaluation metrics, and produce task-adaptive compressed models while attempting to retain generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system-level toolkit—combining logit matching, representation alignment, ensemble or multi-teacher signals, data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), and complementary compression techniques—KD frequently preserves much of a teacher’s performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and attention to robustness and bias transfer. Practical deployment therefore requires matching the distillation recipe to task requirements, student capacity, and data realities.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A range of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and procedural variants—multi-teacher schedules, online/self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware pipelines—enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success hinges on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, choosing appropriate training data or synthesis strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). KD also has well-documented failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distribution shift) that require tailored remedies. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative applications, practical recommendations, and open challenges for using KD as an integrated compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses information from large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The approach has diversified from soft-label matching into a toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or combinations thereof; it can be adapted to settings with limited or no access to original training data, and it is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and integrating KD into a broader compression pipeline that validates robustness and fairness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Across vision, language, retrieval, and graph domains, KD is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—enables substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical application requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: The Central, Practical, and Conditional Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of techniques for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. KD methods span soft-target matching, intermediate representation and layer-wise alignment, ensemble-to-single transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-conscious pipelines. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that approach teacher performance across NLP, speech, and vision tasks, and that combining KD with architecture-aware compression or augmentation strategies often yields the best trade-offs. However, KD has limits: student capacity, the availability and quality of distilled data, and inherited teacher biases can all constrain outcomes. Responsible and effective compression therefore requires selecting the appropriate distillation signals, considering task and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or fairness-aware objectives).

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behaviors and internal signals. A broad family of KD methods—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, and data- or task-aware variants—has been applied across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment typically combines KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires attention to data availability, teacher–student alignment, and robustness or fairness concerns. Open challenges include principled handling of teacher errors, data-free distillation, and reliable transfer of robustness and fairness properties.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft logits to a rich family of techniques that enable deployment of large models in resource-constrained settings. Across NLP, vision, generative modeling, and cross-modal systems, distillation methods that match intermediate representations, adapt teacher signals to student inputs, exploit many-to-many layer correspondences, and combine with pruning or ensemble guidance consistently produce compact models with near-teacher performance. KD is also effective for domain adaptation and continual learning, making it a practical foundation for producing small, fast, and robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, architecture-aware transformations, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, teacher and student architecture, data availability, and optimization. Practical pipelines combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact models, data augmentation, pruning/quantization, and task-aware objectives) and must address challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, robustness preservation, and faithful transfer of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate representation imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and adaptive-teacher schemes, data- and domain-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how teacher quality and data regimes affect outcomes, and what practical trade-offs remain. Open problems center on robustness to domain shift and adversaries, distillation without original data, and automated, architecture-agnostic pipelines for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, mature toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Approaches vary from transferring softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, from online and multi-teacher schemes to data-free and privacy-aware pipelines. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and other modalities shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while delivering substantial reductions in inference cost, parameter count, and memory footprint. Practical success depends on matching distillation targets and schedules to student capacity and deployment constraints, handling limited or private data appropriately, and addressing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable efficient deployment. Beyond simple logit matching, KD methods include intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when distillation objectives, student capacity, and data strategies are carefully matched; however, success depends on addressing optimization and representation mismatch, data availability, teacher imperfections, and fairness or robustness concerns. Effective pipelines combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training schedules to balance efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and providing regularization—that together enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. KD integrates naturally with other compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization), supports data-free and privacy-sensitive settings, and scales across modalities and deployment constraints. At the same time, effective distillation requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle imperfect teachers and data mismatch, and when to combine KD with complementary techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe and offers practical, evidence-based recommendations for deploying KD in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to which teacher signals are transferred, how the student is initialized, and how complementary compression methods are integrated, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a magic bullet: theoretical and empirical work highlights optimization gaps, failures under heterogeneous data or federated settings, and robustness and rare-token fidelity issues. Realistic deployment therefore requires task-aware distillation recipes, student pre-training, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but large neural models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Research has developed a spectrum of approaches — from matching logits to feature-level imitation, structural transformation of architectures, multi-teacher schemes, and task-specific adaptations — and has applied them across domains including detection, generative modeling, recommendation, retrieval, and multiple NLP tasks. Empirical work highlights both opportunities (substantial parameter reductions, faster inference, retained or modestly degraded accuracy) and pitfalls (propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, robustness concerns), motivating targeted algorithmic adjustments such as selective distillation, projector modules, and adversarially-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Vaughan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Empirical work across vision and NLP shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective distillation is typically a system-level design problem that combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student, how to prepare or synthesize data, and which complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to apply. Practical success hinges on handling capacity mismatch, data availability, distribution shift, and transferred biases; hybrid pipelines that adapt signals and data to the student and task deliver the most reliable trade-offs between compactness and performance.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective engine for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. KD’s flexibility—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-teacher schedules, and operating with or without original data—makes it the practical backbone of compression pipelines. However, distillation can amplify teacher biases, struggle with rare-token or long-tail behavior, and depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; practitioners should therefore adopt integrated, task-aware KD workflows combined with complementary compression techniques and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When implemented beyond simple soft-label matching — e.g., via intermediate-feature alignment, layer-mapping, task-aware objectives, curriculum-driven sample selection, or privacy-preserving synthesis — KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost and enabling on-device, federated, or low-latency deployment. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategy, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Best practice treats KD as one element in a compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture search, and targeted evaluation for adversarial and distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for turning large, high‑performing neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment under memory, latency, data, and privacy constraints. A range of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure), alignment strategies (layer-wise matching, attention-mediated projection, task-aware filtering), and training regimes (multi-teacher ensembles, online/self-distillation, or adversarial setups) have been developed to trade off compression with retained performance. Across modalities, well-designed distillation pipelines—often combined with complementary compression methods or student pretraining—yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy while enabling real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for transferring capabilities from large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or modality-limited models. When combined with complementary strategies—domain adaptation, feature-level matching, data augmentation, and meta-learning—distillation enables practical deployment across constrained devices, heterogeneous federated systems, and domain-shifted settings. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization subtleties and mismatches between teacher and student require methodological care and, in some cases, alternative regularization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power from larger, high-capacity models (teachers or ensembles) into smaller, efficient models (students) while preserving accuracy and generalization. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (logits) to imitating intermediate representations, designing student-friendly teachers, handling limited or no access to original training data, and tailoring distillation to task-specific architectures (e.g., detection, reinforcement learning, recommender systems). Practical concerns include privacy, computational cost at training or inference, multi-teacher integration, and the role of pre-training for compact models. Empirical results across vision, language evaluation, medical imaging, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning show that appropriately chosen distillation objectives and training regimes can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering large savings in storage and latency.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Flexible — but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods have matured into a practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. These techniques have been applied across domains (vision, speech, NLP, healthcare), settings (offline compression, federated learning, continual adaptation), and architectures (ensembles, transformers, detectors, GANs). However, their success depends on factors such as the availability and nature of data used for distillation, domain mismatch between teacher and student, robustness and privacy requirements, and optimization dynamics. KD can unlock high-performing compact models when combined with task-aware design choices (e.g., feature imitation, augmentations, architecture search, or ensemble teachers), but practitioners must account for trade-offs and failure modes to use it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Engineering Requirements
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students. Empirical work across vision, speech, ranking, and natural language tasks shows KD can deliver large reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s predictive power. However, KD is not an automatic solution: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how the teacher is prepared, student architecture and pretraining, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires engineering KD into a broader compression pipeline that addresses data, robustness, fairness, and optimization concerns.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. Over the past decade these methods have evolved from logits-based soft-label transfer to a wide range of strategies including feature- and attention-matching, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols, and adaptations for few-shot or federated settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines can retain much of teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost; however, effectiveness depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and practical constraints such as privacy, communication, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe: by transferring teacher signals at multiple levels, combining input-side strategies, and integrating complementary compression methods, KD enables compact models that meet practical deployment constraints. Effective distillation requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices about what to transfer. When deployed with these design principles, KD substantially narrows the performance gap between large teachers and efficient students while remaining adaptable to privacy, federated, and heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD enables deployment under latency, storage, and privacy constraints by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals from teacher to student. When treated as a configurable toolkit — choosing which teacher signals to transfer, how to align representations, and which complementary compression methods to apply — distillation yields efficient models that are practical for real-world NLP and vision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression — Claims, Mechanisms, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—soft-output transfer, intermediate-representation alignment, and relational objectives—and is most powerful when composed with complementary techniques such as architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data-centric strategies. While KD frequently preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can enable real-world deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints, it is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, teacher errors, and rare-token or safety-critical behaviors create failure modes that require methodical mitigation. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core element of a wider compression pipeline, adopt task- and data-aware choices about what to transfer, and evaluate students on distributional, robustness, and application-specific criteria.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is multifaceted—able to transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble behavior—and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity and initialization, teacher quality and alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and robustness considerations. A pragmatic, system-level KD pipeline that combines representation-level supervision, student pretraining, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression steps offers the most reliable route to compact, performant models across modalities and deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Pipeline Design, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most usefully viewed as a system-level, modular pipeline for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When KD combines soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, selective or synthesized data, multi-teacher aggregation, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery), it reliably yields small students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of transferred biases and domain shifts. Practical deployments therefore require principled choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and which data strategies to apply.
