papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. The technique has diversified into a family of methods (logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free and federated variants) and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and augmentation to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on matching distillation strategy to goals (latency, privacy, robustness) and on careful handling of teacher quality, student capacity, and available data.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable transfer of predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include internal-representation distillation, module replacement, self-distillation, selective sample transfer, and adaptations for constraints such as privacy, communication, and low-precision inference. Applied across domains—from NLP rankers and translation to graph, vision-language, and speech systems—these methods trade off fidelity, efficiency, and robustness through a variety of algorithmic and engineering solutions.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe: by transferring teacher signals at multiple levels, combining input-side strategies, and integrating complementary compression methods, KD enables compact models that meet practical deployment constraints. Effective distillation requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices about what to transfer. When deployed with these design principles, KD substantially narrows the performance gap between large teachers and efficient students while remaining adaptable to privacy, federated, and heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile suite of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment of distilled models depends on matching the distillation recipe to task constraints (data availability, teacher–student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and privacy or communication limits) and frequently benefits from multi-stage or task-aware distillation schedules. While KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance, open issues remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable methods for distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, and Evolving Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core engineering and research paradigm for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving accuracy and desirable behaviors. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, ensemble-to-single compression, and complementary data- and architecture-aware techniques. When treated as a design problem—choosing which signals to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data constraints—KD enables deployment across resource-limited and domain-shifted settings, but open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect teachers, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching teacher logits to a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models suitable for deployment and adaptation in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and task-specific properties (e.g., robustness or privacy signals), and it is most effective when combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, data-side interventions, and low-precision or structured pruning. Success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, how to construct or augment distillation data, and how to adapt teacher behavior; practical pipelines treat KD as one component of a broader compression workflow rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a set of teacher→student techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large models into smaller, faster, or privacy-preserving students. Across vision and NLP, KD variants include soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and feature-level imitation, relational or structure-preserving losses, multi-teacher ensembles, data-agnostic or data-free procedures, and self- or cross-supervised transfer. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design choices, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing compact models but requires careful handling of data regimes, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and robustness or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable tool for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving (or even improving) performance. Beyond straightforward teacher→student logit matching, KD can be applied structurally (transforming architectures without redesign), combined with quantization, used for domain adaptation of large pretrained language models, leveraged in multi-teacher and few-shot settings, and operated without access to original data. KD’s benefits arise both from transferring predictive behavior and from inducing effective regularization; when paired with careful choices (e.g., feature projectors, divergence measures, or pseudo-replay for data-free settings), KD enables deployment of compact, reliable models across vision, speech, language, graph, and generative-model domains.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central tool for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers to smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a system—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—it delivers large practical wins in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving most task performance. Responsible use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Deployment Pathways
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language. KD transfers behavior at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure) and, when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data and training choices, enables substantial reductions in latency and memory with modest loss in task performance. However, realizing these gains in practice requires attention to optimization, teacher–student capacity alignment, data complexity and provenance, and robustness under distribution shift or privacy constraints. Emerging directions—online distillation for distributed training, KD-aware federated strategies for heterogeneous devices, and continual or domain-adaptive distillation—expand KD’s applicability but also raise open research questions about preserved behaviors and propagated biases.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained environments. KD encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and structural or layer-wise mappings. Its practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and protocols to teacher and student architectures, the availability and nature of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD can preserve much of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, degraded robustness under domain shift, and optimization challenges that require task-aware design and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relational information. It is a flexible, task-aware toolkit used to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical distillation pipelines combine choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, features, relations), how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to supply or synthesize data, often together with complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization. Distillation has been applied successfully across modalities—language, speech, vision, and combinatorial problems—yet performance depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases; these constraints motivate adaptive, multi-stage, and privacy-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models for deployment. KD operates by transferring useful behavior from a trained teacher to a compact student and can work through matching outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble signals. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), careful teacher–student alignment, and data strategies that address limited or private training data. KD yields strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) but has failure modes tied to student capacity, data mismatch, and propagation of teacher biases; production use therefore requires design-sensitive recipes and monitoring for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. A family of methods—matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and synthesizing or selecting data—enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Success in real systems depends on task-aware design, careful teacher–student pairing, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable paradigm for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD methods—ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and relational structure—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and whether to complement distillation with adversarial or ensemble signals. When these elements are chosen and tuned for task and deployment constraints, KD produces compact models that are effective in resource-limited and application-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable transferring performance from large, often pre-trained or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster student models for practical deployment. The literature converges on a flexible toolkit: matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations or relations, using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or generated data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization). Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks when designers choose appropriate distilled signals, align heterogeneous architectures, and address data constraints; remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, distilling under no- or limited-data regimes, preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller or specialized models. KD can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate layers, and features), can be combined with model pruning and precision reduction, and can support domain adaptation and on-device deployment. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on how teacher knowledge is represented and transferred, the choice of data and augmentations used during distillation, and the deployment context (e.g., heterogeneous federated environments). When methods for intermediate-layer alignment, feature mimicking, data-side regularization, and architecture-aware mapping are combined thoughtfully, KD yields compact, efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s performance while enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal representations. Across vision, speech, NLP, and generative modeling, KD variants (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free approaches) enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher’s task performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and robustness/fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Poole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD unifies a family of training objectives and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, adversarially chosen examples, and privacy- or task-aware pipelines—that can be composed with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. When designed with attention to teacher–student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD enables practical, high-quality compression across NLP and vision tasks while exposing research needs around robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft targets into a unifying toolkit that enables model compression, deployment on constrained devices, privacy-aware release, and modality transfer. By combining architectural mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and data-free or federated setups, KD can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while drastically reducing footprint and computation. This makes KD essential for translating state-of-the-art large models into real-world, resource-limited, and privacy-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, higher-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). In practice KD has been applied to compress large pre-trained language models, enable fast inference in NLP, adapt models to new domains or tasks, support heterogeneous and federated settings, and enable data-free scenarios. Approaches differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single vs multi-teacher, jointly trained teachers), and how training data is used or synthesized. Empirical results show KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of task performance, but success depends on choices around layer mapping, feature vs. logit supervision, data complexity, and training protocols. Open challenges include handling data heterogeneity, optimizing teacher-student pairings, and ensuring stable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques form a flexible toolkit for turning large, accurate deep models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners transfer information at output (soft targets), intermediate representations (features or attention maps), or relational/ensemble signals and often combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and architecture-aware design. Success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized inputs), and addressing risks such as propagation of teacher errors, fairness and robustness degradation, and performance loss on rare or distribution-shifted phenomena. Across vision and language, careful combinations of distillation objectives, student pretraining or co-design, and complementary compression techniques enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while retaining much of teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, and Evolving Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core engineering and research paradigm for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving accuracy and desirable behaviors. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, ensemble-to-single compression, and complementary data- and architecture-aware techniques. When treated as a design problem—choosing which signals to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data constraints—KD enables deployment across resource-limited and domain-shifted settings, but open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect teachers, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted framework for transferring knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods span soft-label matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfers, and data-side strategies including augmentation and synthetic or data-free inputs. When integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance; however, practical use requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core and a Bounded Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware objectives, intermediate representation alignment, appropriate data strategies (including synthetic-data approaches), and architecture-aware design, KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. However, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, and optimization fragility—that demand complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful protocol design to realize reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted training paradigm that enables compact, deployable models by transferring aspects of teacher models to smaller students. When treated as a central tool rather than a single recipe, KD supports a range of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), deployment modalities (on-device, federated, data-limited), and complementary compressions (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to adapt data and curricula; with these considerations KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though optimization subtleties and robustness remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer predictive behavior from large, expensive models to smaller, faster models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade research has produced a taxonomy of distillation mechanisms (logit/soft-target matching, representation or feature imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers), adaptations for low-data or data-free settings, and combinations of distillation with architecture search and pruning. Empirical work shows that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance at large computational savings, but also highlights practical failure modes: students often do not perfectly match teacher predictive distributions, optimization choices and training data matter strongly, and specialized methods are needed for task-specific or distributed scenarios. Recent advances emphasize multi-stage/multi-teacher schedules, augmentation-aware objectives, online distributed training, and loss formulations that better capture teacher uncertainty; combining these approaches with automated architecture search and structured pruning yields stronger, hardware-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Pre-training, Task-Awareness, Privacy, and Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large language models into smaller, faster students for NLP applications. Its effectiveness depends not only on the student-teacher framework but on complementary practices: pre-training compact models, aligning distilled signals to task-relevant representations, handling limited or private data, leveraging multiple teachers when available, and explicitly distilling for robustness. When these elements are combined and tuned, distillation yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, System-Level Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed as a flexible, system-level toolbox that transfers predictive behavior and intermediate structure from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free procedures), KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving most of the teacher’s utility. However, its success is conditional: practitioner choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, and data regime materially affect outcomes; KD is not a universal fix for robustness, domain shift, or bias propagation. I argue that KD should be applied as an integrated engineering practice with clear evaluation of limits and targeted remedies for the known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed to match student capacity, task requirements, and available data, distillation reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its practical success depends on selecting appropriate distilled signals (logits, features, relations), combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, architecture search, quantization), and addressing open problems such as data scarcity, teacher error transfer, and robustness across distributions.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning: Necessity, Challenges, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models and transferring desirable properties (accuracy, robustness, or representations) into smaller, deployable students. In NLP and related deep-learning domains, distillation enables the efficient use of pretrained teachers, supports domain adaptation and continual learning, and can be adapted for supervised, self-supervised, and adversarial objectives. However, naive distillation can degrade specific behaviors (e.g., lexical choices or uncertainty calibration) unless the distillation pipeline addresses alignment of inputs and representations, intermediate-layer supervision, the sample-wise effects of soft labels, and robustness transfer. I argue that distillation should be treated as a design problem—choosing which knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and when to expose students to raw or adversarial signals—to yield compact models that preserve both accuracy and desirable inductive properties.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior and representations from a teacher to a student. Methods span matching teacher output distributions (soft labels), aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, adversarial or data-free approaches, and online or federated variants that trade communication and privacy constraints against fidelity. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage imperfect or heterogeneous data and devices, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression strategies (e.g., pruning or architecture search). While distilled students often retain much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency or resource constraints, open challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, handling domain shift and robustness, and designing privacy- and communication-efficient protocols for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Constraints, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models retain much of the utility of high-capacity systems. KD operates across levels of abstraction (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure) and is routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (quantization, pruning, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation, or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many settings, but success is context-dependent: it depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, or robustness. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, practical variants, and actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Its effectiveness depends not only on transferring final outputs but also on choosing what knowledge to transfer (samples, internal representations, or layers), preparing students (pre-training or architecture search), and combining distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision arithmetic). However, distillation is not a panacea: optimization difficulties and imperfect teachers can limit how closely students match teachers and how much generalization benefit is obtained. Careful, task-aware design and hybrid pipelines produce the most reliable gains.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical, Conditional Endorsement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are indispensable tools for deploying high-capacity deep models in resource- and latency-constrained settings. When combined with architecture-aware strategies, task adaptation, and data-aware protocols, KD recovers much of teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and size reductions. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: optimization difficulties, domain and low-frequency token mismatches, privacy or data-availability constraints, and fairness concerns require tailored remedies. Effective compression thus integrates KD with architecture search, progressive replacement, data-free methods, and fairness- and federated-aware training to achieve reliable, deployable students.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system — combining softened-output matching, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning or quantization — KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, addressing data-availability constraints, and mitigating risks from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. I argue KD should be the default component of production compression pipelines provided practitioners adopt task-aware recipes, incorporate data-aware and architecture-aware remedies, and monitor robustness and fairness outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Takeaways
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-faceted toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining much of task performance. KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, alignment of intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free strategies. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is tailored to student capacity, data regime, and downstream robustness or fairness requirements. Open problems include reliable distillation without original data, principled handling of teacher errors and biases, and transferring robustness and rare-behavior performance to compact students.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a practical, multimodal toolkit that reliably shrinks large models into deployable students while preserving much of their utility. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD delivers substantial gains in latency, memory, and communication efficiency. However, safe and effective use of KD requires careful, task-aware choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle data scarcity or privacy limits, and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or student pretraining. This paper argues KD should be the default engine for model compression in deep learning and NLP, outlines its key mechanisms, highlights practical limitations and failure modes, and provides concrete recommendations for robust, deployed KD pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques reduce the size and runtime of large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to a smaller student model. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, methods vary in what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, relations, or latent experts), how training data are used (original data, distilled predictions, or no data), and how multiple or imperfect teachers are combined. Practical adaptations include task-specific losses, sample selection or weighting, and architectural transformations; KD is also integrated with system-level strategies such as federated learning and pruning to meet device constraints. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing compute and memory, but success depends on choices of teacher strength, data availability, multi-teacher aggregation, and whether task structure (e.g., localization or ranking) is explicitly addressed.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Necessary Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure via soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention maps, and relational objectives. When integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful data and architecture design, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance and enable latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained deployment. However, KD’s benefits are contingent on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher artifacts, and distributional shift; addressing these requires deliberate, task-aware pipelines and evaluation tailored to real-world constraints.
