papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been widely adopted to reduce model size and runtime while retaining performance. Work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows multiple complementary strategies—logit matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and self-distillation—can be effective alone or in combination. Practical success depends on choices about teacher strength, student architecture, pre-training, and optimization, and recent systems integrate distillation with pruning, low-precision, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. A rich set of techniques—soft-target (logit) transfer, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive replacement, data-free or zero-shot distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—has emerged. Practical success depends on choices about teacher signals, student architecture and capacity, data availability and augmentation, and integration with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and rare behaviors, and operating under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques include matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or relational structure, and ensembling or online schemes. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and can serve beyond compression as an implicit regularizer, an enabler of domain adaptation, and a mechanism for privacy-aware release. Effectiveness depends on choices about teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture mapping, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and targeted interventions to preserve robustness and mitigate undesirable transferred behaviors. A task- and deployment-aware KD pipeline that selects what and how to transfer—sometimes staged or hybridized with complementary compression primitives—yields the most reliable real-world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a flexible and central mechanism for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. The literature frames KD as a family of objectives — soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate representation matching, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures — which are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while drastically reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or absent training data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch and robustness issues. Task-aware and architecture-aware adaptations (including layer-wise filtering, task-adaptive architecture search, and transformer-specific compression) have proven effective in producing compact models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a practical, multimodal toolkit that reliably shrinks large models into deployable students while preserving much of their utility. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD delivers substantial gains in latency, memory, and communication efficiency. However, safe and effective use of KD requires careful, task-aware choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle data scarcity or privacy limits, and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or student pretraining. This paper argues KD should be the default engine for model compression in deep learning and NLP, outlines its key mechanisms, highlights practical limitations and failure modes, and provides concrete recommendations for robust, deployed KD pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical method to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, faster students, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with sensible pre-training, representation-level supervision, adaptive teacher strategies, and complementary compression techniques; but it is not a universal solution and can fail when data are limited, teacher and student representations mismatch, or optimization is poorly designed. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox—applied carefully, combined with other compression methods, and adapted to domain or system constraints—to deliver reliable, high-quality compressed models for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed as a multifaceted training paradigm that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Far from being a single trick, KD encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. When matched to task constraints—data availability, architecture mismatch, privacy needs—and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource targets. However, practitioners must address optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatches, and domain-shift or low-frequency behavior to reliably deploy distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, flexible toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep learning and NLP models. KD encompasses multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure), can be combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and is effective across modalities when matched to task and data constraints. Its practical use requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, the choice and provenance of distillation data, and measures to avoid propagating teacher weaknesses (e.g., errors, bias, or fragility). When applied with task-aware design and complementary methods, KD yields small models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements; however, responsible deployment requires remedies for robustness, fairness, and domain-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression: Evidence, Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse signals—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure—and because those signals can be adapted to constraints such as data scarcity, architecture mismatch, or privacy. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to address teacher errors and optimization instabilities. The best outcomes arise from integrated distillation pipelines that combine representation-level objectives, careful data strategies (including augmentation or synthetic samples), architecture-aware mapping, and multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules tailored to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescriptive Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a central toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware or data-free strategies, and integration with other compression primitives—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of rare behaviors; realizing reliable compressed models requires deliberate teacher preparation, student-aware design, data or synthesis strategies, and explicit robustness and bias interventions.

papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the core of a hybrid, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: Effectiveness, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When combined with complementary practices—task-aware signal selection, intermediate representation alignment, pretraining for compact architectures, multi-teacher or self-distillation, and data augmentation or synthesis—KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, fairness concerns, and theoretical gaps constrain its effectiveness in some settings. Careful design choices and hybrid pipelines are therefore required to realize reliable compression in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a diverse toolkit for transferring information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more constrained models. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, altering training curricula, and designing compression-aware teachers or architectures. These approaches have been applied across domains including vision, speech, translation, retrieval, and on-device deployment, and have been adapted to privacy- and communication-constrained settings. Empirical and analytical work has clarified different mechanisms by which distillation aids learning, and recent work explores automation, adversarial feature transfer, sample selection, and architecture-aware strategies to improve efficiency without sacrificing much performance.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Constraints, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models retain much of the utility of high-capacity systems. KD operates across levels of abstraction (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure) and is routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (quantization, pruning, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation, or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many settings, but success is context-dependent: it depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, or robustness. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, practical variants, and actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware, and Privacy-Conscious Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment across modalities and tasks. Effective KD goes beyond naive logits matching: task-aware layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware search can preserve accuracy while reducing compute and memory. Moreover, self-distillation and teacher-free variants reduce dependence on strong teachers, and specialized KD variants address scarce data, privacy, and federated constraints. These directions together form a roadmap for applying KD in real-world deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behavior — and by combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, and architecture search — KD enables substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of a teacher’s performance. However, its effectiveness depends on design choices: what signals are distilled, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Treating KD as a configurable, system-level toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the most reliable path to compact, high-quality models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile, practically oriented set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure, and is most effective when combined with complementary practices such as pre-training compact students, careful selection or synthesis of distillation data, teacher scheduling, and architecture-aware alignment. Empirical work shows KD routinely enables meaningful latency and memory reductions with modest accuracy loss, but success depends on principled design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; these considerations motivate task-aware pipelines and ongoing research into robustness, fairness, privacy, and theoretical underpinnings.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints by trading modest amounts of accuracy for substantial reductions in compute and footprint. When treated as an engineering toolkit—combining output-level supervision, intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware strategies—KD reliably produces compact models that meet real-world constraints; success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity and attention to optimization, data selection, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable tool for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving (or even improving) performance. Beyond straightforward teacher→student logit matching, KD can be applied structurally (transforming architectures without redesign), combined with quantization, used for domain adaptation of large pretrained language models, leveraged in multi-teacher and few-shot settings, and operated without access to original data. KD’s benefits arise both from transferring predictive behavior and from inducing effective regularization; when paired with careful choices (e.g., feature projectors, divergence measures, or pseudo-replay for data-free settings), KD enables deployment of compact, reliable models across vision, speech, language, graph, and generative-model domains.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool for Compression — Powerful When Combined, Limited When Used Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and many-to-many layer mapping. In practice, KD reliably improves student efficiency and often preserves much of teacher behavior, but it has predictable failure modes — e.g., propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to teacher–student mismatch, and dependence on data quality and augmentation — that require complementary practices such as student pretraining, careful teacher design, data augmentation, and hybrid compression (pruning/quantization).

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression: when applied as an integrated, task-aware system it enables compact students that preserve much of a teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware surgery), careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols), and explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment and robustness evaluation. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits are conditional on signal selection, data and initialization choices, and evaluation for fairness and domain-shift resilience. I argue for treating KD as a configurable pipeline (signals, data, architecture, optimization) and for adopting specific practices that mitigate common failure modes in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression (and When to Combine It)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact deep and NLP models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD delivers consistent accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across modalities, improves small-model representations, and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not always sufficient on its own: success requires careful choice of transfer signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity and architecture, and integration with complementary compression, data, or training procedures to preserve rare or safety-critical behaviors. I argue that KD should be treated as the central element of a compression toolkit, applied pragmatically with domain- and deployment-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation targets, preparing the student (often via pre-training), and addressing data, privacy, and robustness constraints—KD yields compact models that retain a substantial fraction of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks. However, its success depends on design choices (what to distill and when), data availability, and mitigation of teacher errors; thus KD is best treated as a system of complementary techniques rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple logit-based supervision to richer representation-, relation-, and adversarial-level transfers and is used to enable on-device inference, multi-task models, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and data-limited deployments. Best outcomes arise when KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), task-aware design, careful sample or synthetic-data strategies, and interventions for bias and privacy. KD has clear empirical benefits across modalities but also well-documented limits—sensitivity to data availability and heterogeneity, potential propagation of teacher errors or biases, and the need for architectural and optimization care—motivating principled adaptations and further study.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware, and Privacy-Conscious Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment across modalities and tasks. Effective KD goes beyond naive logits matching: task-aware layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware search can preserve accuracy while reducing compute and memory. Moreover, self-distillation and teacher-free variants reduce dependence on strong teachers, and specialized KD variants address scarce data, privacy, and federated constraints. These directions together form a roadmap for applying KD in real-world deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. KD methods extend beyond matching softened teacher outputs to include representation- and layer-wise transfer, multi-teacher and ensemble schemes, data- and architecture-aware designs, and combinations with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical and conceptual work shows KD both transfers teacher predictive behavior and acts as an inductive regularizer; practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, whether and how to pre-train compact students, and how to handle limited or private data, robustness, and rare-token phenomena. Remaining challenges motivate refinements in data synthesis, principled layer mapping, robustness preservation, and methods that respect privacy and heterogeneous deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Starting Point for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Scope, Complementary Needs, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, first-line method for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both vision and NLP. KD reliably delivers large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when applied as a flexible toolkit (soft targets, intermediate feature transfer, attention/relational objectives, online/self-distillation) and when integrated with data-aware practices and complementary compression techniques. At the same time, KD is not sufficient by itself: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability and provenance, architecture and capacity alignment, and explicit interventions to preserve robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical pipelines therefore begin with KD but must plan for targeted architectural adaptation, quantization/pruning, data strategies (filtering, synthesis, or data-free methods), and careful evaluation under domain shift and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a composable pipeline and combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data strategies, KD routinely produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, distillation has clear limits—optimization failures, propagation of teacher errors, and issues under heterogeneous or data-limited regimes—that require targeted remedies and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques shrink large neural models into smaller, faster models for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. A diverse set of approaches—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or generative sample synthesis—has emerged across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention maps, or structural priors), how to align heterogeneous architectures, whether teacher or student are adapted during training, and how to handle limited or absent training data. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost are possible with modest performance loss, but open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robustness under domain shift, privacy, and closing optimization/capacity gaps between teachers and students.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD can preserve predictive performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its strengths derive from a variety of mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-feature alignment, layer-mapping, and task-adaptive architecture design — and from being combinable with complementary compression techniques. However, realizing consistent gains requires careful choice of distilled targets, attention to representation alignment between teacher and student, and explicit handling of data-, fairness-, and robustness-related risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox of targeted interventions rather than a single recipe, and provides concise, evidence-based recommendations for practitioners compressing models in vision and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Flexible Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit: it can transfer logits, internal representations, or structured relational knowledge; it can be combined with architecture search, multi-teacher schemes, or data synthesis; and it can be adapted with task-aware filtering or teacher-aware training to address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. Carefully chosen distillation targets, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression components produce small, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core—and Bounded—Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search)—KD routinely enables deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and evaluation of robustness and fairness; thus KD should be treated as a central element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Benefits, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of methods for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce parameter count, inference latency, and resource use while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive performance. KD techniques operate at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and are commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical work shows KD enables effective on-device and domain-specialized deployment, supports data- and privacy-constrained scenarios, and can be adapted to multi-modal or cross-domain transfers. However, KD’s practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and match to deployment domain, student capacity and architecture, and optimization design; these factors create failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, domain shift) that require hybrid pipelines and careful validation.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Partial Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile means to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their teacher performance. In practice KD enables latency- and memory-constrained deployment, supports continual and domain adaptation, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet engineering constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and requires task-aware alignment of signals and data strategies (including privacy-preserving or data-free approaches) to realize consistent benefits. I argue KD should be treated as a flexible toolkit that is integrated with task-aware layer mapping, privacy and data strategies, and complementary compression methods to produce robust, high-utility compressed models for NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a single recipe but a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large models into compact students suitable for deployment. When combined with task-aware architecture choices, ensemble or self-generated signals, and orthogonal compression methods, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Careful attention to what is distilled, data strategy, and training dynamics mitigates common failure modes and enables robust, real-world compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms (output matching, representation mimicry, and relational objectives), and when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and teacher adaptation) it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD is therefore best treated as a composable toolkit: powerful in practice but requiring careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or sensitive data.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft targets into a unifying toolkit that enables model compression, deployment on constrained devices, privacy-aware release, and modality transfer. By combining architectural mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and data-free or federated setups, KD can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while drastically reducing footprint and computation. This makes KD essential for translating state-of-the-art large models into real-world, resource-limited, and privacy-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing models to smaller, efficient models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has diversified beyond simple teacher→student logit-matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, online and federated protocols, teacher-free and data-free variants, and architectural co-design. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D perception, and NLP demonstrates that carefully chosen distillation signals, layer mappings, and training practices (e.g., pretraining, projected feature matching, selective sample weighting) produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance; remaining challenges include data heterogeneity, privacy, robustness, and automating teacher–student pairing and signal selection.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. KD has become a practical engine for deploying deep and NLP models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on design choices—what teacher signals to transfer, how to align layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to adapt teacher or student architectures—and on combining distillation with complementary compression methods. Empirical evidence shows KD works across classification, detection, generation, retrieval, and domain-adaptive settings, while remaining challenges include data-free scenarios, heterogeneous architectures and devices, robustness and fairness preservation, and optimization/capacity mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression, Regularization, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a flexible, multi-purpose methodology rather than only a compression trick. KD enables smaller, efficient models for deployment, but it also serves as a mechanism for learned regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release. Practical success relies on matching the distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), the teacher selection and scheduling, and the data or data-generation strategy to the deployment constraints. Combining logits-based supervision with representation-level objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware query mechanisms produces more reliable and robust student models for real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller or specialized models. KD can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate layers, and features), can be combined with model pruning and precision reduction, and can support domain adaptation and on-device deployment. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on how teacher knowledge is represented and transferred, the choice of data and augmentations used during distillation, and the deployment context (e.g., heterogeneous federated environments). When methods for intermediate-layer alignment, feature mimicking, data-side regularization, and architecture-aware mapping are combined thoughtfully, KD yields compact, efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s performance while enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Contemporary Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across computer vision and natural language processing, a wide family of distillation strategies—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, many-to-many layer mappings, and task-aware layer selection—has been developed to trade off accuracy, latency, and model size for practical deployment. Empirical work shows that combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware transformations) and adapting distillation signals to task and data constraints yields compact models that capture much of teacher performance. At the same time, distillation must contend with capacity mismatch, robustness and distribution-shift sensitivity, privacy concerns, and the need for principled layer- and signal-alignment strategies—areas that motivate continued methodological and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies condense large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision students suitable for deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has produced a taxonomy of approaches—soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate/feature imitation, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher fusion, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling substantial gains in inference speed and memory; theoretical analyses attribute much of KD’s benefit to regularization from soft targets and the transfer of inductive biases. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors, operating without original training data, and designing adaptive, task-aware distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. It is a practical toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, to adapt models across domains, and to support privacy-aware or federated settings. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and language tasks shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers are configured, and how training is regularized materially affect the trade-offs between efficiency and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across computer vision, speech, multimodal, and NLP tasks, distillation protocols—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature and attention-based transfers—enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Success depends on careful choices of distillation targets, teacher-student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, low-precision, architecture search, or federated protocols) it yields deployable models for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Not Sufficient Tool for Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial runtime, memory, and latency gains while preserving much of predictive performance. KD is effective across modalities and deployment regimes, but its success depends on careful method choice, teacher quality, data availability, and combination with complementary compression strategies. Future progress requires deeper theoretical understanding, better automation for heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive settings, and principled integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. A spectrum of techniques — matching softened outputs, aligning features or attention, layer-mapping (including many-to-many mappings), multi-teacher or ensemble transfers, and data-free or generator-based synthesis — enables large reductions in size and latency while largely preserving task performance. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and training choices; but it faces practical challenges including capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the potential transfer of teacher biases or adversarial vulnerabilities.
