papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, flexible toolbox for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure) and naturally composes with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its practical value lies in enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but realizing those gains requires careful teacher–student design, signal selection, data management, and attention to capacity and distributional mismatch. When applied with representation-aware objectives and hybrid compression pipelines, KD routinely delivers robust trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency while exposing concrete research and engineering challenges around rare-event behavior, teacher error propagation, and data-limited regimes.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavioral or representational information from a teacher to a student. Across computer vision and NLP, distillation methods vary from matching output soft targets to aligning internal representations, performing self-distillation, and synthesizing or selecting data when original training examples are unavailable. Empirical work shows distillation can retain much of teacher performance while enabling domain adaptation, improved generalization, and deployment under latency or memory constraints. However, effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, layers, features), the availability and complexity of training data, regularization (e.g., label smoothing and augmentation), and fairness or privacy constraints. Open challenges include understanding when students can outperform teachers, balancing bias mitigation and utility, and combining distillation with pruning or hardware-aware compression for edge deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Best Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a comprehensive, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision and natural language tasks. When designed as a system—selecting appropriate teacher signals, leveraging intermediate representations, using data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, distillation has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, propagation of teacher errors) and open research needs (reliable data-free methods, robustness and fairness preservation, principled teacher selection). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central engineering primitive for practical model compression, and it outlines evidence-based best practices and remaining research priorities to make distillation robust for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression — Powerful but Incomplete
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable approach for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a core component of compression pipelines, KD often yields substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a standalone cure: its success depends on what signals are distilled, student capacity and initialization, data availability and distributional match, and safeguards against propagating teacher errors or biases. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as the default starting point that must be combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware mapping), robust data strategies, and careful evaluation of edge cases and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints by trading modest amounts of accuracy for substantial reductions in compute and footprint. When treated as an engineering toolkit—combining output-level supervision, intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware strategies—KD reliably produces compact models that meet real-world constraints; success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity and attention to optimization, data selection, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. The field encompasses softened-logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, online and multi-teacher schemes, data-free or data-limited techniques, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery. Empirical work shows KD often improves deployment trade-offs in vision, speech, and language tasks, but its reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and nature of distillation data, and interventions to mitigate optimization, robustness, and fairness issues. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable toolkit—selecting objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to match task and deployment constraints—and continue to explore theory and methods that address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for translating large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. Treated as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD combines soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, relational or contrastive objectives, and data-side interventions to produce compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires matching distillation objectives to student capacity and task requirements and combining KD with complementary compression techniques and careful data strategies. Despite its practicality, KD has limits—data scarcity or privacy, capacity mismatch, teacher errors, and robustness under distributional shift—that must be managed through design choices and complementary methods.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques form a flexible toolkit for turning large, accurate deep models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners transfer information at output (soft targets), intermediate representations (features or attention maps), or relational/ensemble signals and often combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and architecture-aware design. Success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized inputs), and addressing risks such as propagation of teacher errors, fairness and robustness degradation, and performance loss on rare or distribution-shifted phenomena. Across vision and language, careful combinations of distillation objectives, student pretraining or co-design, and complementary compression techniques enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while retaining much of teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Research has extended KD from simple soft-target matching to a toolbox of representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance in practice, but success depends on choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, data availability, and optimization; open problems include principled teacher selection, handling limited or no data, robustness to teacher errors, and aligning compression with hardware and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Nuanced Path to Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques to transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary strategies — such as pre-training compact architectures, data augmentation, selective sample transfer, and module-level compression — KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what is transferred, the availability and nature of data, teacher–student design, and optimization choices. Responsible deployment requires understanding both the practical strengths (efficiency, adaptability, applicability to privacy settings) and the limitations (data dependence, optimization gaps, possible degradation on rare or shifted inputs) of distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical, Conditional Endorsement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are indispensable tools for deploying high-capacity deep models in resource- and latency-constrained settings. When combined with architecture-aware strategies, task adaptation, and data-aware protocols, KD recovers much of teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and size reductions. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: optimization difficulties, domain and low-frequency token mismatches, privacy or data-availability constraints, and fairness concerns require tailored remedies. Effective compression thus integrates KD with architecture search, progressive replacement, data-free methods, and fairness- and federated-aware training to achieve reliable, deployable students.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central—but Not Sufficient—Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for shrinking ensembles into a broad, adaptable paradigm for producing deployable deep and NLP models. KD methods transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, and online or self-distillation, and they are most effective when combined with task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD alone faces practical limits—data and domain mismatch, capacity gaps between teacher and student, and the need to preserve rare or safety-critical behaviors—so practitioners should treat KD as a central component of a compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a practical, multimodal toolkit that reliably shrinks large models into deployable students while preserving much of their utility. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD delivers substantial gains in latency, memory, and communication efficiency. However, safe and effective use of KD requires careful, task-aware choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle data scarcity or privacy limits, and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or student pretraining. This paper argues KD should be the default engine for model compression in deep learning and NLP, outlines its key mechanisms, highlights practical limitations and failure modes, and provides concrete recommendations for robust, deployed KD pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It is a flexible toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, and to support privacy- and data-constrained settings. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to the student capacity and task, choosing appropriate data or synthetic surrogates when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Key open problems include capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and principled design of teacher–student schedules.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment constraints. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, appropriate data strategies, and careful teacher–student design. While KD frequently yields compact models that retain most teacher performance and can improve robustness or enable low-precision inference, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—making KD a powerful but context-sensitive tool rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible suite of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while often retaining most task performance. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s effectiveness across modalities and tasks, but also reveals systematic limitations arising from teacher-student capacity mismatch, optimization difficulties, data heterogeneity, and the sample-wise effects of soft targets. To make distillation reliably useful in production and research, practitioners should pair KD with task-aware layer selection, representation-level supervision, careful sample weighting, and complementary compression methods such as pruning or quantization. This balanced approach preserves KD’s deployment advantages while mitigating its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Centrality, Mechanisms, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of a broader compression pipeline—combining choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—KD can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, its effectiveness is conditional: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, capacity limits, and risks of propagating teacher errors or biases require task-aware recipes and complementary techniques to produce reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. It has evolved from straightforward soft-label training to richer objectives that match features, attention, or module behaviors, and to deployment-aware variants that address privacy, data scarcity, and heterogeneous devices. Empirical work across vision and language shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation signals, data, and architecture choices are carefully matched; important open problems include data heterogeneity, capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and theoretical understanding of what is actually transferred.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching soft teacher outputs into a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models across vision and language. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can transfer final predictions, intermediate representations, relational structure, and inductive biases from large teachers to smaller students, and it is often most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to data constraints (real-data, augmented, or data-free regimes). Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher-student alignment, and data; remaining challenges include teacher imperfections, distributional mismatch, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques that compress large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students for deployment in constrained settings. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention transfer, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and teacher-free or data-synthesizing approaches. When combined with complementary compression practices (pre-training compact architectures, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation), KD often preserves most of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy requirements. However, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, data availability and distributional shift, and mitigation of propagated biases or robustness gaps. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common failure modes, and practical design patterns shown to improve distillation outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile methodology for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a system—combining choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), teacher and student architecture design, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, or structural transforms)—KD produces efficient models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its strengths include broad applicability across modalities, regularizing benefits from soft targets, and empirical gains when paired with representation-level objectives; its limits arise from capacity mismatch, potential transfer of teacher errors or biases, distribution shift, and challenges when original training data are unavailable. A production-ready pipeline therefore uses KD as a central component but couples it with careful signal selection, student-aware teacher design, data synthesis or rehearsal mechanisms, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search or data augmentation—enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical successes span classification, object detection, machine translation, and language-model compression, but practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to curate or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. The method’s effectiveness arises partly from the regularizing properties of soft targets and richer teacher signals, yet distillation can propagate teacher errors and struggle with capacity, data heterogeneity, and robustness unless augmented by task-aware design or additional engineering.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened logits to a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern distillation transfers output behavior, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble knowledge; can operate with limited or no access to original training data; and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. Practical application requires matching the distillation recipe to task requirements, student capacity, and data availability while managing teacher imperfections and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and accelerates large neural models by transferring information from one or more teacher models into a smaller student. Across vision and language, KD variants extend from logit-matching to feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher ensembling, online/co-distillation, privacy-aware and federated setups, and combinations with quantization or structured pruning. Practical pipelines combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, domain adaptation, and task-specific pretraining to obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Despite empirical success across modalities and deployment settings, trade-offs remain in teacher selection, information type to transfer, stability for heterogeneous architectures, and theoretical interpretation of what is transferred; these motivate further research into adaptive teacher weighting, feature alignment layers, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, resource-efficient models from larger teachers across computer vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. As a modular system, KD supports multiple information-transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, and architecture search). Real-world deployment requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or no access to teacher data, and how to address robustness and fairness concerns. When KD is applied as a deliberate toolchain—selecting task-aware objectives, incorporating multi-teacher or synthetic-data protocols, and combining with data- and model-level compression—practical students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Open problems remain around preserving rare-event behaviors, domain shift, and student-aware teacher shaping, which motivate focused research on curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power from larger, high-capacity models (teachers or ensembles) into smaller, efficient models (students) while preserving accuracy and generalization. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (logits) to imitating intermediate representations, designing student-friendly teachers, handling limited or no access to original training data, and tailoring distillation to task-specific architectures (e.g., detection, reinforcement learning, recommender systems). Practical concerns include privacy, computational cost at training or inference, multi-teacher integration, and the role of pre-training for compact models. Empirical results across vision, language evaluation, medical imaging, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning show that appropriately chosen distillation objectives and training regimes can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering large savings in storage and latency.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Centrality, Mechanisms, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of a broader compression pipeline—combining choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—KD can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, its effectiveness is conditional: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, capacity limits, and risks of propagating teacher errors or biases require task-aware recipes and complementary techniques to produce reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring teacher behavior through output probabilities, intermediate representations, or structured signals and by combining distillation with data strategies and complementary compression primitives, practitioners can achieve large reductions in memory, latency, and compute while retaining most of the original performance. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires attention to data availability, teacher–student alignment, fairness and bias risks, and task- or hardware-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression (and When to Combine It)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact deep and NLP models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD delivers consistent accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across modalities, improves small-model representations, and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not always sufficient on its own: success requires careful choice of transfer signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity and architecture, and integration with complementary compression, data, or training procedures to preserve rare or safety-critical behaviors. I argue that KD should be treated as the central element of a compression toolkit, applied pragmatically with domain- and deployment-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies aim to transfer predictive behavior from larger or more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient ones. The literature shows a variety of mechanisms (soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature alignment, progressive module replacement, adversarial feature matching), data- and training-focused interventions (data selection, augmentation, mixup, control of dataset complexity), and hybrid combinations with pruning or ensembling. Empirical results across NLP and vision tasks indicate that KD can preserve much of teacher performance while accelerating inference, but success depends strongly on (a) the choice of distillation targets and layer mappings, (b) the complexity and provenance of the distillation data, and (c) complementary techniques such as pre-training, feature-level matching, or structured pruning. Practical approaches therefore tailor the distillation recipe to model capacity, task characteristics, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. A rich family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free or federated variants—have been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture design to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on the choice of distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, availability and quality of data (or synthetic alternatives), and complementary training or architectural strategies. Key limitations remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and principled teacher selection, and ongoing work targets federated and privacy-sensitive settings as well as methods that pre-train compact students before distillation.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi-Purpose Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a broad, practical toolbox rather than a narrow compression trick. Beyond shrinking parameter counts, KD can regularize learning, transfer intermediate and structural knowledge, enable model adaptation when data are limited or private, preserve robustness and fairness properties, and support cross-modal or modality-restricted deployment. Realizing these benefits in deep learning and NLP requires combining complementary signals (soft targets, feature/attention matching, and relational losses), adapting teacher schedules and layer mappings to student capacity, and integrating KD with data synthesis or multi-teacher strategies when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to improve efficiency while retaining performance. Methods span logits-based soft-label transfer, feature- or layer-wise matching, adversarial and data-free distillation, architecture-aware projection or search, and task-adaptive compression for NLP. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision, speech, generative models, and language models; recent theory clarifies when and why soft labels help and when mixing hard labels matters. Practical designs—attention-guided layer alignment, projectors or ensembles of projectors, and careful data augmentation or synthetic-data generation—substantially affect student quality. Open challenges include data-privacy constraints, distillation across heterogeneous architectures, preserving teacher errors, and better theoretical/empirical guidance for designing KD pipelines for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single recipe for copying teacher logits into a central, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and behaviors of larger teachers. KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational structure), how they handle data availability (data-rich, data-free, federated), and how they combine with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments select and tune KD components to match modality, data-privacy constraints, and latency or memory budgets.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and structured-data domains. The field spans matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, multi-teacher and staged schedules, and privacy- or data-constrained variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in latency, memory, and deployment feasibility; success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, student architecture and capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Open challenges include principled handling of imperfect teachers, distributional and robustness limits, privacy guarantees, and automating design choices for diverse tasks and devices.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed as a multifaceted training paradigm that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Far from being a single trick, KD encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. When matched to task constraints—data availability, architecture mismatch, privacy needs—and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource targets. However, practitioners must address optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatches, and domain-shift or low-frequency behavior to reliably deploy distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Task-Aware Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach that should serve as the central mechanism for compressing large deep models into deployable students when matched to task constraints. KD is not a single recipe: it spans soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, relational objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free protocols. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pretraining of compact models, pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and when practitioners attend to data provenance, teacher–student alignment, and robustness/fairness risks, KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Best practice emphasizes task-aware design, careful selection of distillation signals, and explicit interventions for domain shift, privacy, and rare-event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation offers a practical route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness arises from multiple distillation signals (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention or channel maps) and from combining distillation with pre-training, architecture-aware design, and data-management strategies. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires explicit choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited, private or heterogeneous data.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practical Patterns, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relational signals. A broad set of techniques—soft-target matching, representation- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, self- or data-free distillation, and integration with pruning/quantization or architecture adaptation—enables large reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate data; predictable failure modes include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and transfer of teacher errors or biases. Practical deployment treats KD as an engineering toolkit that must be adapted to task, data, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated with complementary practices such as pre-training, architecture-aware design, data-side strategies, and other compression techniques. However, its success is conditional on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher errors or biases. Treating KD as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the best results for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in NLP: Capabilities, Extensions, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning models for NLP and related domains. When combined with complementary strategies—pretraining of compact models, layer-matching techniques, targeted data augmentation, robustness-aware objectives, privacy-aware protocols, and adaptive teacher training—distillation can produce small models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting deployment constraints.
