papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing deep models and transferring capabilities across architectures and modalities. KD has enabled large speedups and model-size reductions while preserving or even improving downstream task performance when carefully applied. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and distributional heterogeneity, and it can transmit teacher biases or errors. Combining logit-based supervision with feature- and relation-focused objectives, aligning intermediate representations, and adapting distillation strategies to task and data constraints yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD enables practical trade-offs among accuracy, latency, privacy, and data availability by varying what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps), how it is transferred (layer-wise, channel-wise, adversarial), and which complementary compression strategies are applied (pruning, architecture search, quantization). When combined with techniques for limited or absent access to original training data, KD supports few-shot, zero-shot, and privacy-respecting workflows that make deployment feasible across modalities and resource constraints. Successful application requires selecting appropriate distilled signals and curricula, and often integrating KD with task- and architecture-specific methods.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a logits-matching trick into a broad set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. Modern KD variants transfer soft predictions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structure; they are combined with data-centric practices (augmentation, synthetic and zero-shot data) and complementary compression (pruning, architecture search) to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains in NLP (notably transformer compression) as well as vision, graphs, and federated settings, while theoretical and empirical studies reveal optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and distributional/heterogeneity limitations. Practical pipelines favor pretraining or progressive replacement, representation-level matching, task-adaptive data strategies, and awareness of privacy and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation enables deployment of powerful pretrained models in resource-constrained settings, supports specialization (e.g., task or domain adaptation), and can be combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search) to produce practical, production-ready models. Advances in distillation methodology — including multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, teacher meta-learning, and task-aware layer-wise alignment — address fundamental challenges of capacity mismatch, information selection, and optimization stability, leading to more robust and efficient student models. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of any production-focused compression pipeline for deep learning and NLP systems, and that research emphasis on better teacher–student dynamics and task-aware transfer will yield the largest practical gains.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi-Purpose Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a broad, practical toolbox rather than a narrow compression trick. Beyond shrinking parameter counts, KD can regularize learning, transfer intermediate and structural knowledge, enable model adaptation when data are limited or private, preserve robustness and fairness properties, and support cross-modal or modality-restricted deployment. Realizing these benefits in deep learning and NLP requires combining complementary signals (soft targets, feature/attention matching, and relational losses), adapting teacher schedules and layer mappings to student capacity, and integrating KD with data synthesis or multi-teacher strategies when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A range of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and procedural variants—multi-teacher schedules, online/self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware pipelines—enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success hinges on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, choosing appropriate training data or synthesis strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). KD also has well-documented failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distribution shift) that require tailored remedies. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative applications, practical recommendations, and open challenges for using KD as an integrated compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal representations. A rich set of mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature or representation imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers, and data-free or privacy-aware strategies—has been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher accuracy while substantially reducing latency and footprint, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, data and augmentation strategies, teacher quality, and training schedules. Ongoing work focuses on robustness to domain shift, heterogeneous devices, limited or unavailable data, and principled ways to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a flexible and central mechanism for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. The literature frames KD as a family of objectives — soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate representation matching, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures — which are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while drastically reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or absent training data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch and robustness issues. Task-aware and architecture-aware adaptations (including layer-wise filtering, task-adaptive architecture search, and transformer-specific compression) have proven effective in producing compact models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. KD encompasses multiple information channels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and is commonly used together with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data (real, augmented, or synthesized). While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can serve additional roles such as regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release, it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain shift, and propagation of teacher errors—that necessitate careful pipeline design and complementary methods for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescriptive Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a central toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware or data-free strategies, and integration with other compression primitives—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of rare behaviors; realizing reliable compressed models requires deliberate teacher preparation, student-aware design, data or synthesis strategies, and explicit robustness and bias interventions.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is multifaceted—able to transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble behavior—and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity and initialization, teacher quality and alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and robustness considerations. A pragmatic, system-level KD pipeline that combines representation-level supervision, student pretraining, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression steps offers the most reliable route to compact, performant models across modalities and deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and structured-data domains. The field spans matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, multi-teacher and staged schedules, and privacy- or data-constrained variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in latency, memory, and deployment feasibility; success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, student architecture and capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Open challenges include principled handling of imperfect teachers, distributional and robustness limits, privacy guarantees, and automating design choices for diverse tasks and devices.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practices, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Across vision and natural language processing, KD has become a flexible toolkit—combining logits/soft-targets, feature- or layer-level matching, data-side strategies (augmented or synthetic data), and architecture-aware student design—to produce compact models that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. Empirical work demonstrates meaningful efficiency gains in settings ranging from BERT compression to non-autoregressive translation, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary compression (architecture search, pruning, quantization) and from addressing optimization, privacy, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, flexible toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep learning and NLP models. KD encompasses multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure), can be combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and is effective across modalities when matched to task and data constraints. Its practical use requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, the choice and provenance of distillation data, and measures to avoid propagating teacher weaknesses (e.g., errors, bias, or fragility). When applied with task-aware design and complementary methods, KD yields small models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements; however, responsible deployment requires remedies for robustness, fairness, and domain-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression with Clear Limits and Research Priorities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision, speech, and language. KD combines multiple signals (soft-labels, intermediate representations, attention and feature matching, synthetic-data generation) and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods. However, its practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, access to appropriate data (or robust data-free methods), and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and fairness risks. This paper argues that KD should remain central to compression pipelines while research focuses on principled teacher selection, reliable data-free distillation, representation-aware objectives, and safeguards for privacy and bias.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing deep models for real-world deployment. KD unifies multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational/attention matching) and interoperates naturally with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data synthesis). Properly designed KD pipelines—choosing what to transfer, mapping teacher and student representations, and addressing data or privacy constraints—yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across classification, generation, detection, and language tasks. At the same time, KD has limits (capacity mismatch, optimization and data mismatch, and potential propagation of teacher biases), so production pipelines must combine KD with pretraining, data strategies, and robustness/fairness checks to be reliable.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single training trick but a central, practical framework for compressing large models into deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-label transfer, representation-level alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and integration with other compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate design: choosing which teacher signals to transfer, addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, and using data-aware or data-free strategies when original training data are unavailable. I argue that KD should be the core component of any production-focused compression pipeline, paired with representation-level objectives and careful data strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: The Practical Power and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable and practical approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster, and—in many cases—more deployable models. When combined with complementary techniques (pre-training of compact architectures, pruning, low-precision numerics, or data-free synthesis), distillation can retain much of a teacher model's performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. However, the success of distillation is conditional on choices about teacher-student design, access to data or surrogates, and optimization strategies; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple logit-based supervision to richer representation-, relation-, and adversarial-level transfers and is used to enable on-device inference, multi-task models, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and data-limited deployments. Best outcomes arise when KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), task-aware design, careful sample or synthetic-data strategies, and interventions for bias and privacy. KD has clear empirical benefits across modalities but also well-documented limits—sensitivity to data availability and heterogeneity, potential propagation of teacher errors or biases, and the need for architectural and optimization care—motivating principled adaptations and further study.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable transferring performance from large, often pre-trained or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster student models for practical deployment. The literature converges on a flexible toolkit: matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations or relations, using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or generated data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization). Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks when designers choose appropriate distilled signals, align heterogeneous architectures, and address data constraints; remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, distilling under no- or limited-data regimes, preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, practical approach that compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behaviors, internal representations, or relational structure. Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that a tailored combination of distillation targets, architectural alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning) yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints; however, success depends on careful design to avoid capacity mismatch, data or distributional mismatch, and unintended transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression techniques compress or replace large pretrained models with smaller, efficient models while aiming to retain much of the original performance. Modern work spans logit-based soft-label distillation, feature- and attention-based representation matching, layer-wise and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation schemes, meta-learned teachers, and approaches for resource- or data-constrained scenarios (including data-free and few-shot settings). Applications include compressing large language models into lightweight architectures for deployment, accelerating visual and multimodal models, enabling distributed training, and improving robustness and transfer. Key challenges include selecting what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align heterogeneous architectures, preventing capacity mismatch and overfitting, and preserving task-relevant information while removing redundant representations. Empirical strategies that combine representation-level losses, task-aware selection, and online or meta-learning mechanisms tend to yield the best tradeoffs between efficiency and retained accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible engineering paradigm for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what teacher signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data- or curriculum-driven strategies to use—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's task performance. Effective deployment requires pairing distillation with complementary compression methods, pretraining or adaptation of compact architectures, and explicit attention to limits such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from one or more teacher models to a student model. Methods range from matching output distributions (soft logits) to aligning internal representations, using ensembles or multiple teachers, conducting distillation without access to original data, and employing self-distillation or teacher-adaptation strategies. Empirical work across vision and language shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data constraints determine the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much teacher performance when paired with task-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques. Its success, however, depends on decisions about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, access to data or synthetic surrogates, and mitigation of robustness and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Research has produced a rich set of mechanisms (soft-targets, representation- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives), data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, and data-free surrogates), and complementary compression steps (pruning, architecture search, quantization). Empirical evidence shows that KD frequently recovers most teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, data choices, and addressing capacity, optimization, and robustness limits.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Engineering Requirements
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students. Empirical work across vision, speech, ranking, and natural language tasks shows KD can deliver large reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s predictive power. However, KD is not an automatic solution: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how the teacher is prepared, student architecture and pretraining, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires engineering KD into a broader compression pipeline that addresses data, robustness, fairness, and optimization concerns.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, and generative tasks. KD methods extend beyond simple output (logit) matching to include intermediate-representation and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, curriculum and data-aware schedules, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and tuned for teacher–student compatibility and data constraints, KD frequently produces compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Nonetheless, challenges remain in handling capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of rare or tail behaviors, teacher errors and biases, and reliably distilling without access to original data—areas that motivate ongoing research in curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Partial Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile means to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their teacher performance. In practice KD enables latency- and memory-constrained deployment, supports continual and domain adaptation, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet engineering constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and requires task-aware alignment of signals and data strategies (including privacy-preserving or data-free approaches) to realize consistent benefits. I argue KD should be treated as a flexible toolkit that is integrated with task-aware layer mapping, privacy and data strategies, and complementary compression methods to produce robust, high-utility compressed models for NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. KD methods extend beyond matching softened teacher outputs to include representation- and layer-wise transfer, multi-teacher and ensemble schemes, data- and architecture-aware designs, and combinations with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical and conceptual work shows KD both transfers teacher predictive behavior and acts as an inductive regularizer; practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, whether and how to pre-train compact students, and how to handle limited or private data, robustness, and rare-token phenomena. Remaining challenges motivate refinements in data synthesis, principled layer mapping, robustness preservation, and methods that respect privacy and heterogeneous deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. A family of methods—matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and synthesizing or selecting data—enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Success in real systems depends on task-aware design, careful teacher–student pairing, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a heuristic into a set of principled, modality-agnostic techniques that enable deployment of high-capacity models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. By transferring predictive behaviour and internal representations from large teachers to compact students, distillation preserves much of the teacher's utility while enabling large speed, memory, and communication gains. Recent advances show that combining representation-level matching, teacher–student co-design, data-free synthesis, and task-adaptive compression yields robust, practical pipelines for compressing models across vision, language, graph, and federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, feature maps, or distilled data. Applications span model compression for deployment (including transformer compression for NLP), multimodal model adaptation, federated and resource-constrained learning, and improving robustness or fairness. Practical strategies include layer-wise or attention-based projection, progressive module replacement, adversarial and data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations that account for data heterogeneity and inductive bias.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: Effectiveness, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When combined with complementary practices—task-aware signal selection, intermediate representation alignment, pretraining for compact architectures, multi-teacher or self-distillation, and data augmentation or synthesis—KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, fairness concerns, and theoretical gaps constrain its effectiveness in some settings. Careful design choices and hybrid pipelines are therefore required to realize reliable compression in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical strengths derive from multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, relational objectives, and data-side strategies—that together enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, propagation of teacher errors) and design choices (what to transfer, how to align layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to select or weight teachers) substantially affect outcomes. The most reliable deployments treat KD as one component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines task-aware loss design, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches), architecture-aware mapping, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning or quantization.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Integrated Feature-, Data- and Robustness-aware Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from simple logit matching into a toolbox of complementary techniques. Empirical and theoretical work shows that (1) matching internal features often transfers richer representations than logits alone, (2) the choice of input-side interventions (e.g., data augmentation) substantially changes distillation dynamics, and (3) robustness, teacher quality, and sample selection must be addressed explicitly. I argue that effective model compression in deep learning and NLP requires integrating feature-level mimicry with careful input-space design, selective or confidence-weighted teacher signals, and robustness-aware objectives. This combined approach maximizes student performance while keeping models compact and deployment-ready.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained environments. KD encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and structural or layer-wise mappings. Its practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and protocols to teacher and student architectures, the availability and nature of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD can preserve much of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, degraded robustness under domain shift, and optimization challenges that require task-aware design and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable efficient deployment. Beyond simple logit matching, KD methods include intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when distillation objectives, student capacity, and data strategies are carefully matched; however, success depends on addressing optimization and representation mismatch, data availability, teacher imperfections, and fairness or robustness concerns. Effective pipelines combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training schedules to balance efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relationships. Across deep learning and NLP, KD enables deployment of performant models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability and design of distillation data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and training protocols that mitigate capacity and distribution mismatches. Open challenges include robust teacher selection, data- and domain-mismatch, and scaling distillation methods to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Task-Aware Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach that should serve as the central mechanism for compressing large deep models into deployable students when matched to task constraints. KD is not a single recipe: it spans soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, relational objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free protocols. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pretraining of compact models, pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and when practitioners attend to data provenance, teacher–student alignment, and robustness/fairness risks, KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Best practice emphasizes task-aware design, careful selection of distillation signals, and explicit interventions for domain shift, privacy, and rare-event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core — Powerful but Contextual in Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., representation alignment, architecture-aware search, data synthesis, and multi-teacher schedules), but it is not a universal cure: data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency/token behaviors in NLP, and fairness or privacy constraints limit its effectiveness unless practitioners design targeted, hybrid pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a principled and versatile toolkit for compressing, adapting, and scaling deep models in NLP. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from a teacher to a student, KD enables high-quality, resource-efficient models that meet latency and capacity constraints while preserving task performance. Recent work demonstrates KD variants that are task-adaptive, layer-aware, many-to-many, online, and even teacher-free, making KD applicable across domain adaptation, multi-tasking, multimodality, and large-scale distributed training. This paper argues that KD should be viewed not merely as a compression trick but as a unifying framework that links theoretical insights, practical training strategies, and system-level considerations for deploying compact NLP models.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated not as a narrow compression trick but as a unifying, practical paradigm for producing compact, deployable models while preserving accuracy, robustness, and task-specific behavior. KD’s range—spanning soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and adversarial or curriculum-enhanced transfers—makes it uniquely suited to combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. At the same time, KD requires careful design to handle teacher-student mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and data-availability or privacy limits; following representation-aware objectives, adaptive teacher strategies, and hybrid compression pipelines yields the most reliable results.
