papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Best-Practice Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what knowledge to transfer, preparing or pretraining students, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives—distillation often yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization difficulties, teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or mismatched data, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases, adversarial weaknesses) remain important concerns. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be combined with targeted architectural, data, and objective choices that address these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile mechanism to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and matched to task constraints, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Success with KD depends on deliberate choices about what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or missing teacher data, and how to protect robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP systems, but its safe and effective use requires task-aware design and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with complementary methods such as student pretraining, progressive replacement, data synthesis, and fairness- or privacy-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The practice spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, and using multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Effective distillation depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to manage robustness and privacy concerns. While KD often preserves much of a teacher's utility in deployed models, limits remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, rare-token behavior, and principled teacher selection, motivating integrated, multi-level distillation pipelines and further empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relational information. It is a flexible, task-aware toolkit used to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical distillation pipelines combine choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, features, relations), how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to supply or synthesize data, often together with complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization. Distillation has been applied successfully across modalities—language, speech, vision, and combinatorial problems—yet performance depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases; these constraints motivate adaptive, multi-stage, and privacy-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Conditional Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best framed not as a single trick but as the practical core of modern model-compression pipelines: a flexible set of signals and schedules that, when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, yields deployable students that preserve much of teacher utility. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks but its benefits are conditional on student capacity, data availability, teacher quality, and explicit handling of robustness, privacy, and domain-shift risks. A pragmatic KD-centered workflow emphasizes multiple distilled signals, careful layer/representation mapping, data-aware or data-free strategies when necessary, and integration with pruning/quantization or architecture search to produce reliable, efficient models for production.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A range of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and procedural variants—multi-teacher schedules, online/self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware pipelines—enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success hinges on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, choosing appropriate training data or synthesis strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). KD also has well-documented failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distribution shift) that require tailored remedies. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative applications, practical recommendations, and open challenges for using KD as an integrated compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core—and Bounded—Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search)—KD routinely enables deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and evaluation of robustness and fairness; thus KD should be treated as a central element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a diverse toolkit for transferring information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more constrained models. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, altering training curricula, and designing compression-aware teachers or architectures. These approaches have been applied across domains including vision, speech, translation, retrieval, and on-device deployment, and have been adapted to privacy- and communication-constrained settings. Empirical and analytical work has clarified different mechanisms by which distillation aids learning, and recent work explores automation, adversarial feature transfer, sample selection, and architecture-aware strategies to improve efficiency without sacrificing much performance.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Centrality, Mechanisms, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of a broader compression pipeline—combining choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—KD can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, its effectiveness is conditional: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, capacity limits, and risks of propagating teacher errors or biases require task-aware recipes and complementary techniques to produce reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a configurable system rather than a single recipe. By choosing which teacher signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, and applying task- and data-aware strategies (including multi-teacher aggregation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and architecture search), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD delivers practical gains across vision and NLP but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors, mismatching capacities, or degrading robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints by trading modest amounts of accuracy for substantial reductions in compute and footprint. When treated as an engineering toolkit—combining output-level supervision, intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware strategies—KD reliably produces compact models that meet real-world constraints; success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity and attention to optimization, data selection, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deploying large deep models by transferring their predictive behavior or internal structure to smaller, faster models. Research has progressed from soft-label teacher-student training toward richer objectives that match internal representations, feature spaces, and decision boundaries; from data-dependent distillation to data-free and privacy-preserving approaches; and from one-size-fits-all compression to task-adaptive, architecture-aware methods. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across speech, vision, and language tasks when distillation objectives, training data (real or synthetic), and search for efficient architectures are carefully tailored. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, balancing regularization and fidelity, and handling heterogeneous or absent data during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened teacher logits to a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Modern KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relations), operate in varied data regimes (full-data, few-shot, data-free/zero-shot), and are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device and low-latency deployments when practitioner choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression are task- and capacity-aware. However, KD is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, limited or private data, and distribution shift create failure modes that require careful objective design, student pretraining, and evaluation under deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible suite of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while often retaining most task performance. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s effectiveness across modalities and tasks, but also reveals systematic limitations arising from teacher-student capacity mismatch, optimization difficulties, data heterogeneity, and the sample-wise effects of soft targets. To make distillation reliably useful in production and research, practitioners should pair KD with task-aware layer selection, representation-level supervision, careful sample weighting, and complementary compression methods such as pruning or quantization. This balanced approach preserves KD’s deployment advantages while mitigating its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Partial Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile means to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their teacher performance. In practice KD enables latency- and memory-constrained deployment, supports continual and domain adaptation, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet engineering constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and requires task-aware alignment of signals and data strategies (including privacy-preserving or data-free approaches) to realize consistent benefits. I argue KD should be treated as a flexible toolkit that is integrated with task-aware layer mapping, privacy and data strategies, and complementary compression methods to produce robust, high-utility compressed models for NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. The field encompasses softened-logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, online and multi-teacher schemes, data-free or data-limited techniques, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery. Empirical work shows KD often improves deployment trade-offs in vision, speech, and language tasks, but its reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and nature of distillation data, and interventions to mitigate optimization, robustness, and fairness issues. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable toolkit—selecting objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to match task and deployment constraints—and continue to explore theory and methods that address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Pre-training Plus Strategic Distillation: Practical Principles for Compressing Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when combined with deliberate choices about pre-training, the form of knowledge transferred, data manipulation during distillation, and adaptive teacher-student dynamics. Compact models that are pre-trained, trained to mimic both outputs and internal representations, and exposed to carefully designed augmented or mixed inputs can match much of the performance of larger models while meeting deployment constraints. However, compression success depends critically on optimization, data distribution, and task-specific phenomena such as rare-word behavior in sequence generation. I argue that a pragmatic pipeline—pre-train compact architectures, distill soft targets and internal representations, use augmentation/mixing to shape training data complexity, and apply adaptive or meta-learned teacher strategies—offers the best trade-off between efficiency and accuracy for deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When used thoughtfully, KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on which signals are transferred (logits, features, relational information), alignment between teacher and student, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and awareness of teacher imperfections. Combining KD with representation-level matching, task-aware layer alignment, online or federated protocols, and data strategies yields the best trade-offs for real systems.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search or data augmentation—enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical successes span classification, object detection, machine translation, and language-model compression, but practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to curate or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. The method’s effectiveness arises partly from the regularizing properties of soft targets and richer teacher signals, yet distillation can propagate teacher errors and struggle with capacity, data heterogeneity, and robustness unless augmented by task-aware design or additional engineering.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression approaches transform large, high-performance neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to matching intermediate representations, designing task-aware layer mappings, synthesizing or augmenting data for training, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications include compressing pretrained transformers for NLP, improving robustness under domain shift, enabling on-device inference and federated learning with heterogeneous devices, and training non-autoregressive sequence models. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and limitations: distillation can yield compact models with strong accuracy but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability or synthesis of data, and handling low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Practical Centrality and Conditional Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core engineering and research tool to compress large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical results across tasks and modalities show KD can substantially reduce parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, and KD integrates naturally with complementary techniques (low-precision numerics, architecture search, pruning, federated or privacy-aware pipelines). At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and robustness concerns require careful design choices and hybrid strategies. Effective deployment therefore depends on selecting which knowledge to transfer, adapting distillation signals to data and architecture mismatches, and combining KD with targeted algorithmic and system-level adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When tailored to model architecture, task demands, and available data, KD yields compact models that enable real-world deployment across modalities and domains.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across tasks and modalities. KD's benefits arise from multiple mechanisms: transferring soft output distributions, mimicking intermediate features, providing regularization that improves generalization, and enabling compression even when original training data are unavailable. Empirically and theoretically, KD should be treated as a toolbox: select loss forms (logit, feature, relational), augment or synthesize data when needed, and consider joint training of teacher and student or teacher design that is friendly to students. Combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture design), KD helps produce efficient models that retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation unifies multiple strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models while preserving performance. It supports a range of goals — parameter and latency reduction, robustness, interpretability, and privacy-aware deployment — by transferring information from a teacher to a student via soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural/architectural guidance. Practical and research advances show that combining distillation modes (feature-level, output-level, progressive module replacement), data augmentation, and adaptive teacher training yields compact models that approach teacher performance even under limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core and Its Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer information at multiple levels (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), be applied with or without original training data, and be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, the availability and nature of data, and how to handle heterogeneity or robustness concerns. A pragmatic KD protocol blends pre-training of compact architectures, appropriate choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free methods when needed), and complementary compression techniques, while actively addressing teacher weighting and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. KD operates across multiple signal levels — softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational or attention patterns — and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Its practical success depends on task-aware choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or privacy constraints, and architectural mapping; when designed carefully, KD enables compact models that closely approach teacher performance but does not automatically mitigate issues like transferred biases, rare-token degradation, or distributional robustness problems.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been widely adopted to reduce model size and runtime while retaining performance. Work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows multiple complementary strategies—logit matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and self-distillation—can be effective alone or in combination. Practical success depends on choices about teacher strength, student architecture, pre-training, and optimization, and recent systems integrate distillation with pruning, low-precision, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD enables deployment under latency, storage, and privacy constraints by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals from teacher to student. When treated as a configurable toolkit — choosing which teacher signals to transfer, how to align representations, and which complementary compression methods to apply — distillation yields efficient models that are practical for real-world NLP and vision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Work has expanded beyond the original teacher→student soft-label matching to include intermediate-representation imitation, multi-teacher and adaptive-teacher schedules, self- and teacher-free variants, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and privacy-preserving approaches). Empirical and theoretical analyses show KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially lowering latency, memory, and sometimes communication cost; success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data heterogeneity, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Remaining challenges include robustness to domain shift and adversaries, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, automating signal and teacher selection, and reliable operation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible tool for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and optimization difficulties—that require task-aware design choices around what to transfer, which teacher(s) to use, and how to prepare distillation data. A pragmatic pipeline that pre-trains compact models, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively combines KD with other compression steps yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective engine for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. KD’s flexibility—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-teacher schedules, and operating with or without original data—makes it the practical backbone of compression pipelines. However, distillation can amplify teacher biases, struggle with rare-token or long-tail behavior, and depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; practitioners should therefore adopt integrated, task-aware KD workflows combined with complementary compression techniques and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal representations. Across vision, speech, NLP, and generative modeling, KD variants (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free approaches) enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher’s task performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and robustness/fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teachers to a smaller student model. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to rich objectives that align intermediate representations, exploit multiple teachers, search for task-specific student architectures, and generate or synthesize data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, speech, vision, graphs) and combined with other compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and recurring challenges — data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and principled objective design — and suggests strategies to mitigate them in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses the functionality of larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and NLP, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, online and multi-teacher schemes, and task-adaptive architecture search—have enabled deployment of compact models with strong empirical performance while revealing trade-offs in teacher–student alignment, data availability, and robustness. Key open challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, effective data-free distillation, and preserving fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors during compression.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and graph domains, KD has been adapted into many variants — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, progressive module replacement, online/multi-teacher training, and data-free or privacy-aware pipelines — often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation targets, student preparation, and data strategies are chosen carefully. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness is limited by teacher quality, data availability or privacy, teacher–student architectural mismatch, and risks of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies, designing student-aware teacher signals, and accounting for robustness and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relations. A diverse set of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data augmentation or synthesis, and deployment-aware co-design with pruning/quantization—are combined in practice to meet latency, memory, privacy, and communication constraints. While distilled students often recover most of teachers' accuracy, success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods; outstanding challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving long-tail behaviors, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a fundamental, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and natural language processing. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; variants address constraints such as lack of original data, domain shift, low-precision hardware, and heterogeneous architectures. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, or privacy constraints, but success depends on choices about teacher quality, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and training protocols. Current directions emphasize multi-stage distillation, data- and architecture-aware objectives, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and pre-training; open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robust cross-domain transfer, low-resource and data-free scenarios, and preserving fairness and calibration under compression.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavioral or representational information from a teacher to a student. Across computer vision and NLP, distillation methods vary from matching output soft targets to aligning internal representations, performing self-distillation, and synthesizing or selecting data when original training examples are unavailable. Empirical work shows distillation can retain much of teacher performance while enabling domain adaptation, improved generalization, and deployment under latency or memory constraints. However, effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, layers, features), the availability and complexity of training data, regularization (e.g., label smoothing and augmentation), and fairness or privacy constraints. Open challenges include understanding when students can outperform teachers, balancing bias mitigation and utility, and combining distillation with pruning or hardware-aware compression for edge deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Practical NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. A growing body of work shows KD's versatility across modalities (vision, speech, text), deployment regimes (edge devices, distributed training), and model families (transformers, convolutional nets, generative models). Combining richer teacher signals (intermediate representations, attention maps, or learned teacher updates), stronger input-side practices (data augmentation), and complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning) yields robust, efficient students suitable for real-world constraints. This paper argues that distillation should be treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit whose components are chosen to match task constraints, and it highlights promising techniques to improve transfer fidelity, training efficiency, and downstream performance.
