papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Success depends on choosing appropriate distillation strategies that account for model structure, task specificity, data availability, and training dynamics. When tailored—via structural transformations, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer alignment, or data-centric augmentations—distillation consistently produces compact models that approach teacher accuracy and enable real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Necessary Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure via soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention maps, and relational objectives. When integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful data and architecture design, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance and enable latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained deployment. However, KD’s benefits are contingent on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher artifacts, and distributional shift; addressing these requires deliberate, task-aware pipelines and evaluation tailored to real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Conditional Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and mature training paradigm that enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving—sometimes improving—task performance. As a practical tool, KD spans logits matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free and zero-shot schemes, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Its success in deployment hinges on matching distillation recipes to data availability, model capacity, and application constraints; when so matched, KD enables deployable students that recover much of teacher behavior, but predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, teacher errors, privacy and fairness concerns) require complementary methods and careful protocol design.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques convert large, accurate neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained inference environments. Approaches vary from transferring soft-label outputs to aligning intermediate representations, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing data during teacher–student training, and compressing ensembles. Empirical results across speech, language, vision, and graph tasks show that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost; task-adaptive compression and careful design of teacher–student interactions (including training teachers to be student-friendly) further improve student effectiveness. Practical choices—what to distill (logits, features, or structure), how to align mismatched architectures, and how to augment data or leverage ensembles—determine final trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. KD encompasses multiple information channels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and is commonly used together with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data (real, augmented, or synthesized). While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can serve additional roles such as regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release, it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain shift, and propagation of teacher errors—that necessitate careful pipeline design and complementary methods for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy. KD operates through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when combined with task-aware data strategies and complementary compression methods. When designed with attention to what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data, KD enables deployment of compact models across modalities and constraints while exposing important open questions about robustness, bias propagation, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. A diverse set of techniques—matching soft outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mappings, attention- or relation-aware objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or privacy-conscious procedures—have been developed and evaluated across vision, speech, language, and domain-specific settings. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and integration with complementary compression techniques; remaining challenges include domain shift, propagation of teacher errors, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies aim to transfer predictive behavior from larger or more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient ones. The literature shows a variety of mechanisms (soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature alignment, progressive module replacement, adversarial feature matching), data- and training-focused interventions (data selection, augmentation, mixup, control of dataset complexity), and hybrid combinations with pruning or ensembling. Empirical results across NLP and vision tasks indicate that KD can preserve much of teacher performance while accelerating inference, but success depends strongly on (a) the choice of distillation targets and layer mappings, (b) the complexity and provenance of the distillation data, and (c) complementary techniques such as pre-training, feature-level matching, or structured pruning. Practical approaches therefore tailor the distillation recipe to model capacity, task characteristics, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under compute, memory, and latency constraints. KD operates at multiple granularities (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps) and can be combined with complementary compression strategies such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD often recovers much of teacher performance, its practical success depends on careful choices of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategy (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and evaluation of robustness and low-frequency behaviors. I argue that KD should be the central, task-aware component of modern compression pipelines, used in hybrid workflows that integrate representation-aware objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and complementary compression techniques to meet real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Uses, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students for deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. A spectrum of techniques—from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—supports a range of practical trade-offs. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing footprint, but success depends on student capacity, data availability, and careful design choices; important open problems remain around robustness, principled teacher selection, and reliable distillation under heterogeneous or private data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, architecture-aware transformations, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, teacher and student architecture, data availability, and optimization. Practical pipelines combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact models, data augmentation, pruning/quantization, and task-aware objectives) and must address challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, robustness preservation, and faithful transfer of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are central tools for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models that are practical for deployment. A broad repertoire of methods exists—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial and online co-training, and data- or task-aware augmentation—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, but success depends on how teacher signals are represented, what data are used, and how architecture or domain mismatches are addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to data availability, privacy or federated constraints, teacher errors, and optimization stability; promising directions include pre-training compact students, online and federated distillation protocols, and specialized layer- or modality-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression — Claims, Mechanisms, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—soft-output transfer, intermediate-representation alignment, and relational objectives—and is most powerful when composed with complementary techniques such as architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data-centric strategies. While KD frequently preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can enable real-world deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints, it is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, teacher errors, and rare-token or safety-critical behaviors create failure modes that require methodical mitigation. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core element of a wider compression pipeline, adopt task- and data-aware choices about what to transfer, and evaluate students on distributional, robustness, and application-specific criteria.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision with representation-level alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not automatic: its success depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical path to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. A range of KD mechanisms—including soft-target supervision, intermediate feature or attention matching, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and input-side augmentation—enable tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, privacy, and robustness. KD works best when its components are selected and adapted to deployment constraints: student capacity, available (or private) data, domain shift, and adversarial threats. However, important limitations remain, including distributional mismatch between teacher and student inputs, the preservation of robustness and fairness properties, and principled teacher selection. This article argues that a hybrid, constraint-aware KD strategy that combines representation-level transfer, data augmentation, and robustness- or privacy-aware synthesis offers the most reliable route to practical compression in real-world NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teachers to a smaller student model. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to rich objectives that align intermediate representations, exploit multiple teachers, search for task-specific student architectures, and generate or synthesize data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, speech, vision, graphs) and combined with other compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and recurring challenges — data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and principled objective design — and suggests strategies to mitigate them in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Poole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD unifies a family of training objectives and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, adversarially chosen examples, and privacy- or task-aware pipelines—that can be composed with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. When designed with attention to teacher–student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD enables practical, high-quality compression across NLP and vision tasks while exposing research needs around robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core and Its Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer information at multiple levels (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), be applied with or without original training data, and be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, the availability and nature of data, and how to handle heterogeneity or robustness concerns. A pragmatic KD protocol blends pre-training of compact architectures, appropriate choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free methods when needed), and complementary compression techniques, while actively addressing teacher weighting and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. KD has become a practical engine for deploying deep and NLP models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on design choices—what teacher signals to transfer, how to align layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to adapt teacher or student architectures—and on combining distillation with complementary compression methods. Empirical evidence shows KD works across classification, detection, generation, retrieval, and domain-adaptive settings, while remaining challenges include data-free scenarios, heterogeneous architectures and devices, robustness and fairness preservation, and optimization/capacity mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across computer vision, speech, multimodal, and NLP tasks, distillation protocols—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature and attention-based transfers—enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Success depends on careful choices of distillation targets, teacher-student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, low-precision, architecture search, or federated protocols) it yields deployable models for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Research has developed many variants — logits-based soft-labels, feature- and attention-based matching, layer-wise and task-aware filters, self-distillation, and data-free approaches — and applied them across vision, language, recommendation, and healthcare. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the practical benefits (faster inference, lower memory, domain adaptation, interpretability) and core limitations (optimization obstacles, capacity mismatch, distributional effects), motivating techniques that alter what is distilled, how it is matched, and even how teachers are trained to be more amenable to students.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Responses
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural signals. Across vision and NLP, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi- and self-teaching, and combinations with pruning/quantization—enable reduced inference cost and on-device deployment while attempting to retain performance. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD acts both as a route to transfer representational inductive biases and as a form of learned regularization; its success depends on signal choice, data provenance, capacity mismatch, and optimization. Methodological refinements (data augmentation, adversarial or boundary-focused examples, data-free synthesis, teacher design, and divergence choices) address core challenges in practice, but open problems remain around robustness, privacy, fairness, and reliably closing the teacher–student performance gap.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger or more informed models to smaller ones. Methods vary from soft-label supervision and layer mapping to data-free generation, adversarial sample selection, federated and privacy-preserving protocols, and task- or domain-aware adaptation. Empirical results across vision, language, recommendation, and generative modeling show that distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but performance depends sensitively on what information is transferred, how samples are selected, and whether pretraining or task adaptation is used. Practical use favors hybrids that combine architectural search, selective or weighted distillation, and generation or rehearsal strategies when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deploying large pretrained models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students. Methods include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate features or attention maps, layer- and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation, and data-free approaches that synthesize surrogate inputs. Empirical evidence across vision and language tasks shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size, latency, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Remaining challenges center on preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence models, avoiding transfer of biases or adversarial vulnerabilities, and jointly optimizing compression for hardware and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable transferring performance from large, often pre-trained or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster student models for practical deployment. The literature converges on a flexible toolkit: matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations or relations, using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or generated data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization). Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks when designers choose appropriate distilled signals, align heterogeneous architectures, and address data constraints; remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, distilling under no- or limited-data regimes, preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, flexible strategy for compressing and adapting deep models for real-world deployment. When framed as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, teacher ensembles, data-aware synthesis, and architecture-aware compression—KD routinely yields compact students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to address robustness and rare-event behavior; when these are handled explicitly, KD enables reliable, deployable models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and accelerates large neural models by transferring information from one or more teacher models into a smaller student. Across vision and language, KD variants extend from logit-matching to feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher ensembling, online/co-distillation, privacy-aware and federated setups, and combinations with quantization or structured pruning. Practical pipelines combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, domain adaptation, and task-specific pretraining to obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Despite empirical success across modalities and deployment settings, trade-offs remain in teacher selection, information type to transfer, stability for heterogeneous architectures, and theoretical interpretation of what is transferred; these motivate further research into adaptive teacher weighting, feature alignment layers, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Directions for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress large models into lightweight students for deployment. Recent work shows that KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size or computational cost, but gains depend on what knowledge is transferred, how teachers and students are prepared, and the distillation protocol. I argue that (1) transferring richer information than final logits, (2) preparing students with pre-training, (3) augmenting or synthesizing data during distillation, and (4) co-optimizing architecture-aware compression with distillation together form a robust recipe for reliable compression in NLP and other domains. These directions address generalization, data scarcity, and architectural differences, and they are supported by recent empirical and methodological studies across speech, vision, retrieval, and language modeling.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for transferring information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. KD techniques span output-level supervision (soft logits), intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, self- and progressive distillation, and data-free or zero-shot variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, speech, translation, detection, and generation) while enabling on-device and real-time use; success depends on the choice of distillation targets, the match between teacher and student capacity, the availability and quality of data, and appropriate regularization or augmentation during training. Practical deployment typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and privacy-aware mechanisms to produce robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, multi-signal paradigm for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision and language tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level transfer, layer-wise and channel-wise imitation, and architecture-aware compression—are most effective when paired with careful teacher–student design, data interventions, and complementary compression primitives. Important practical limits remain, including capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, robustness and bias transfer, and data-free settings; addressing these requires integrated pipelines that combine KD with pretraining, architecture search, and targeted training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deploying large deep models by transferring their predictive behavior or internal structure to smaller, faster models. Research has progressed from soft-label teacher-student training toward richer objectives that match internal representations, feature spaces, and decision boundaries; from data-dependent distillation to data-free and privacy-preserving approaches; and from one-size-fits-all compression to task-adaptive, architecture-aware methods. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across speech, vision, and language tasks when distillation objectives, training data (real or synthetic), and search for efficient architectures are carefully tailored. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, balancing regularization and fidelity, and handling heterogeneous or absent data during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It can transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, structured relational signals, or ensemble knowledge, and supports data-side strategies including data-free and augmentation-aware schemes. In practice, KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance when its formulation is matched to task constraints, data availability, and student capacity. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or privacy-preserving compression: practitioner success hinges on selecting appropriate distillation signals, addressing teacher–student and data mismatches, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single training trick but a central, practical framework for compressing large models into deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-label transfer, representation-level alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and integration with other compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate design: choosing which teacher signals to transfer, addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, and using data-aware or data-free strategies when original training data are unavailable. I argue that KD should be the core component of any production-focused compression pipeline, paired with representation-level objectives and careful data strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Research has produced a rich set of mechanisms (soft-targets, representation- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives), data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, and data-free surrogates), and complementary compression steps (pruning, architecture search, quantization). Empirical evidence shows that KD frequently recovers most teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, data choices, and addressing capacity, optimization, and robustness limits.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A range of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and procedural variants—multi-teacher schedules, online/self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware pipelines—enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success hinges on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, choosing appropriate training data or synthesis strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). KD also has well-documented failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distribution shift) that require tailored remedies. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative applications, practical recommendations, and open challenges for using KD as an integrated compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened teacher logits to a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Modern KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relations), operate in varied data regimes (full-data, few-shot, data-free/zero-shot), and are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device and low-latency deployments when practitioner choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression are task- and capacity-aware. However, KD is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, limited or private data, and distribution shift create failure modes that require careful objective design, student pretraining, and evaluation under deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical strengths derive from multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, relational objectives, and data-side strategies—that together enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, propagation of teacher errors) and design choices (what to transfer, how to align layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to select or weight teachers) substantially affect outcomes. The most reliable deployments treat KD as one component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines task-aware loss design, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches), architecture-aware mapping, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning or quantization.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft targets into a unifying toolkit that enables model compression, deployment on constrained devices, privacy-aware release, and modality transfer. By combining architectural mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and data-free or federated setups, KD can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while drastically reducing footprint and computation. This makes KD essential for translating state-of-the-art large models into real-world, resource-limited, and privacy-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are central tools for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models that are practical for deployment. A broad repertoire of methods exists—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial and online co-training, and data- or task-aware augmentation—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, but success depends on how teacher signals are represented, what data are used, and how architecture or domain mismatches are addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to data availability, privacy or federated constraints, teacher errors, and optimization stability; promising directions include pre-training compact students, online and federated distillation protocols, and specialized layer- or modality-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD works at multiple levels — soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behaviour — and is most effective when combined with data strategies, teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression such as pruning or quantization. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can regularize student training, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align capacities, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; careful, task-aware protocols are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become central for deploying high-performing deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has developed a spectrum of techniques — from soft-target supervision and intermediate-layer transfer to multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants — and combined distillation with pruning and architecture search to compress large transformers and other architectures. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains (speed, memory, privacy) and fundamental tradeoffs (bias–variance, data heterogeneity, and information loss), pointing to hybrid protocols and adaptive selection of distillation signals as promising directions.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, modality-agnostic approach that enables conversion of large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, relational or structural signals, data augmentation/synthesis, and multi-stage teacher–student schedules—KD yields compact models that retain much of the teacher's effectiveness. Real-world success requires attention to teacher quality, data provenance, architecture alignment, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; with these design choices, KD is a practical backbone for deploying efficient deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation targets, preparing the student (often via pre-training), and addressing data, privacy, and robustness constraints—KD yields compact models that retain a substantial fraction of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks. However, its success depends on design choices (what to distill and when), data availability, and mitigation of teacher errors; thus KD is best treated as a system of complementary techniques rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques compress large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches range from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and using contrastive or projection-based objectives. Practical training choices—such as which layers or features to mimic, how to filter or weight training samples, the role of data augmentation, and whether compact models are pre-trained—strongly affect outcomes. KD has been applied across domains (vision, language, graphs), combined with quantization and low-precision deployment, and adapted for resource-heterogeneous and latency-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights that KD works both by transferring relational/representational knowledge and by providing regularizing soft targets; effective distillation designs balance these mechanisms and tailor the transfer to task and capacity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students) so the students retain much of the teacher utility while fitting deployment constraints. Research has produced a variety of distillation paradigms: logit- and soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise and channel-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, self-supervised distillation, multi-teacher ensembles and domain-aware adaptation. Empirical work shows that combining pre-training for compact architectures with distillation, using task-aware selection of teacher signals, and tailoring distillation to modality- or task-specific structure leads to stronger compressed models. Important open issues include distillation without access to original data, preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models, and closing the capacity gap between teacher and student without over-constraining the student.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.
