papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The practice spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, and using multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Effective distillation depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to manage robustness and privacy concerns. While KD often preserves much of a teacher's utility in deployed models, limits remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, rare-token behavior, and principled teacher selection, motivating integrated, multi-level distillation pipelines and further empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical set of techniques to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, generative modeling, retrieval, and natural language processing, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt models to new domains or privacy constraints. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), how teacher and student are aligned (layer mapping, attention-weighted projection, task-aware filters), and whether original training data are available (data-free and zero-shot approaches). Success depends on careful choices of teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, signal selection, and data or synthetic-sample strategies; when designed appropriately, KD combined with complementary compression (pruning, architecture transforms) yields compact models with strong empirical performance, while important limitations remain (representation mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, low-frequency token coverage).

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while often preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. KD methods range from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable; they have been successfully applied across vision, generative modeling, recommender systems, and large pretrained language models. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to address limited or private data, robustness, and bias—so practitioners must pair KD with task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to get reliable, deployable results.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central tool for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers to smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a system—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—it delivers large practical wins in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving most task performance. Responsible use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Best Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a comprehensive, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision and natural language tasks. When designed as a system—selecting appropriate teacher signals, leveraging intermediate representations, using data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, distillation has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, propagation of teacher errors) and open research needs (reliable data-free methods, robustness and fairness preservation, principled teacher selection). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central engineering primitive for practical model compression, and it outlines evidence-based best practices and remaining research priorities to make distillation robust for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core and Its Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer information at multiple levels (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), be applied with or without original training data, and be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, the availability and nature of data, and how to handle heterogeneity or robustness concerns. A pragmatic KD protocol blends pre-training of compact architectures, appropriate choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free methods when needed), and complementary compression techniques, while actively addressing teacher weighting and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Contextual Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of methods for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations and attention, and they can be combined with data strategies, multi-teacher schedules, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables real-world deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on principled choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate optimization and robustness limits. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a configurable, task-aware system rather than a single recipe, and it provides practical recommendations for designing effective distillation pipelines in NLP and related deep-learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices and Practical Recommendations for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are practical, versatile tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across computer vision, multimodal, and natural language processing tasks, distillation can preserve or approximate teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and latency. Successful distillation strategies go beyond matching final logits: they exploit intermediate representations, task-aware selection of teacher signals, many-to-many layer mappings, and feature-level or adversarial training to transfer richer knowledge. Combining these approaches yields compact models that retain robustness and task performance, and that can be further complemented by pruning or hardware-aware compression for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system — combining softened-output matching, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning or quantization — KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, addressing data-availability constraints, and mitigating risks from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. I argue KD should be the default component of production compression pipelines provided practitioners adopt task-aware recipes, incorporate data-aware and architecture-aware remedies, and monitor robustness and fairness outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression, Regularization, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a flexible, multi-purpose methodology rather than only a compression trick. KD enables smaller, efficient models for deployment, but it also serves as a mechanism for learned regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release. Practical success relies on matching the distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), the teacher selection and scheduling, and the data or data-generation strategy to the deployment constraints. Combining logits-based supervision with representation-level objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware query mechanisms produces more reliable and robust student models for real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques condense information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable ones. Across vision, speech, recommendation, generative models, and natural language processing, practitioners use a mix of logit-based soft-label supervision, feature imitation, data distillation, multi-teacher fusion, curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware search to trade accuracy for latency, memory, or interpretability. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher accuracy while enabling deployment in latency- or resource-constrained settings; theoretical and empirical analyses attribute much of KD’s effectiveness to the regularizing properties of soft targets, while recent extensions explicitly address adversarial robustness, decision-boundary transfer, domain adaptation, continual learning, and task-specific constraints. Remaining challenges include preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors (e.g., low-frequency phenomena), designing teacher-free or data-free alternatives, and building principled curricula and multi-source transfers that maximize student utility in downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Integrated, Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP when it is applied as an integrated, task-aware system. By combining soft-target transfer with representation-level alignment, targeted feature mimicking, data strategies (including synthesis when data are unavailable), and architecture-aware student design, practitioners can produce compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional: student capacity, data availability and complexity, architecture mismatch, and teacher artifacts limit outcomes unless addressed through deliberate pipeline choices and evaluation. This paper argues for a pragmatic KD-centered workflow and highlights key components and cautionary considerations for reliable compression in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal representations. A rich set of mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature or representation imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers, and data-free or privacy-aware strategies—has been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher accuracy while substantially reducing latency and footprint, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, data and augmentation strategies, teacher quality, and training schedules. Ongoing work focuses on robustness to domain shift, heterogeneous devices, limited or unavailable data, and principled ways to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, modality-agnostic toolkit that enables converting large, high-performing models into compact students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations, and when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data strategies it yields practical pipelines for producing efficient models that retain much of teacher utility. However, effective applied distillation requires attention to student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compress large or expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their predictive power. Across vision, speech, ranking, and natural language processing, KD enables deployment of lightweight architectures by transferring dark knowledge, feature-level signals, or ensemble behavior from teacher models. However, distillation success depends on a set of interacting choices—teacher preparation, student architecture, which signals are transferred, data and augmentation strategies, and optimization—so KD is a powerful tool when combined with careful design but not an automatic solution for all compression needs. This paper synthesizes empirical lessons and provides actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in practice.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques form a flexible toolkit for turning large, accurate deep models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners transfer information at output (soft targets), intermediate representations (features or attention maps), or relational/ensemble signals and often combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and architecture-aware design. Success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized inputs), and addressing risks such as propagation of teacher errors, fairness and robustness degradation, and performance loss on rare or distribution-shifted phenomena. Across vision and language, careful combinations of distillation objectives, student pretraining or co-design, and complementary compression techniques enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while retaining much of teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature imitation, relational/attention transfer, and progressive module replacement—and is used together with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical evidence shows that, when designed for the teacher/student pair and deployment constraints, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and storage cost of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original soft-label paradigm to include distillation of internal representations, layer- and channel-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and teacher-student co-design. Applications span vision, NLP, graph models, generative networks, and large-scale distributed training. Recent work also explores distillation for robustness, low-precision deployment, few-shot compression, and federated or multi-device settings. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain in transferring inductive biases, choosing what and when to distill, and preserving attributes such as fairness and adversarial robustness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from one or more teacher models to a student model. Methods range from matching output distributions (soft logits) to aligning internal representations, using ensembles or multiple teachers, conducting distillation without access to original data, and employing self-distillation or teacher-adaptation strategies. Empirical work across vision and language shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data constraints determine the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD enables deployment under latency, storage, and privacy constraints by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals from teacher to student. When treated as a configurable toolkit — choosing which teacher signals to transfer, how to align representations, and which complementary compression methods to apply — distillation yields efficient models that are practical for real-world NLP and vision deployments.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when originals are unavailable, and designing architecture-aware layer mappings. KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and used across modalities (vision, language, generative models) to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and propagation of biases.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Limitations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals. Techniques extend beyond matching teacher logits to include feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, adversarially-generated or adversarially-robust signals, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. These methods enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP tasks (including compressing pretrained transformers), improve efficiency on-device, and can sometimes preserve or even enhance robustness and generalization. Success depends on choices of distillation target, student architecture and capacity, the nature and availability of distillation data, and handling of domain or agent heterogeneity; open issues include transferring robustness reliably, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and principled handling of heterogeneous or private data sources.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, higher-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). In practice KD has been applied to compress large pre-trained language models, enable fast inference in NLP, adapt models to new domains or tasks, support heterogeneous and federated settings, and enable data-free scenarios. Approaches differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single vs multi-teacher, jointly trained teachers), and how training data is used or synthesized. Empirical results show KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of task performance, but success depends on choices around layer mapping, feature vs. logit supervision, data complexity, and training protocols. Open challenges include handling data heterogeneity, optimizing teacher-student pairings, and ensuring stable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for transferring functionality from large, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones across modalities. When properly applied, KD can enable deployment of compact models with competitive accuracy, but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, selection of distilled signals, and complementary compression strategies. This paper synthesizes empirical findings and method-level advances to argue for principled, task-aware KD workflows that mitigate common pitfalls while maximizing compression gains.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core—and Bounded—Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search)—KD routinely enables deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and evaluation of robustness and fairness; thus KD should be treated as a central element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relations. A diverse set of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data augmentation or synthesis, and deployment-aware co-design with pruning/quantization—are combined in practice to meet latency, memory, privacy, and communication constraints. While distilled students often recover most of teachers' accuracy, success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods; outstanding challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving long-tail behaviors, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and versatile tool available today for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and privacy-preserving mechanisms), KD enables production-ready models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization instability, and risks of propagating teacher errors demand task-aware design, careful data handling, and hybrid engineering practices to obtain reliable results in realistic deployments.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-target logit matching into a multifaceted, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD methods transfer outputs, internal representations, relational structure, or ensemble behavior and are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis or privacy-aware protocols to meet deployment constraints. Successful application depends on matching distillation targets and training data to student capacity and task structure while addressing teacher imperfections, domain shift, and privacy or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. A rich set of techniques—soft-target (logit) transfer, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive replacement, data-free or zero-shot distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—has emerged. Practical success depends on choices about teacher signals, student architecture and capacity, data availability and augmentation, and integration with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and rare behaviors, and operating under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, architecture-aware transformations, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, teacher and student architecture, data availability, and optimization. Practical pipelines combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact models, data augmentation, pruning/quantization, and task-aware objectives) and must address challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, robustness preservation, and faithful transfer of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Practical Priorities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students that are suitable for real-world deployment. When treated as a flexible toolkit and combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, KD reliably reduces memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, data limitations, domain shift, and rare-token or safety-critical behaviors require careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be the default first-line approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students, provided it is applied as a design-sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe. When practitioners treat KD as a modular system—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, leveraging pre-training for compact students, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—they routinely obtain compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and data-availability constraints. Success requires attention to capacity mismatch, data provenance, and robustness/fairness trade-offs; addressing these systematically enables KD to serve as a reliable path from research-scale teachers to production-ready students.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. A rich family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free or federated variants—have been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture design to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on the choice of distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, availability and quality of data (or synthetic alternatives), and complementary training or architectural strategies. Key limitations remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and principled teacher selection, and ongoing work targets federated and privacy-sensitive settings as well as methods that pre-train compact students before distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, modular technique in modern model-compression pipelines: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller students while remaining flexible enough to combine with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-side interventions. KD’s practical success depends on deliberate choices—what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to evaluate robustness and long-tail behavior. When used as part of a system that addresses optimization, data, and mismatch issues, KD frequently yields compact models that meet deployment constraints; when used alone or carelessly it can underperform or propagate undesirable behaviors. The remainder of this paper argues for KD as the default, central component of compression toolkits while outlining its limits and concrete design recommendations to mitigate them.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Research has developed many variants — logits-based soft-labels, feature- and attention-based matching, layer-wise and task-aware filters, self-distillation, and data-free approaches — and applied them across vision, language, recommendation, and healthcare. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the practical benefits (faster inference, lower memory, domain adaptation, interpretability) and core limitations (optimization obstacles, capacity mismatch, distributional effects), motivating techniques that alter what is distilled, how it is matched, and even how teachers are trained to be more amenable to students.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and empirically effective family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and deployment constraints, KD enables moving from research-stage, high-capacity architectures to resource-efficient models suitable for latency- and privacy-constrained production. Realizing KD's full potential requires attention to teacher quality, data and domain mismatches, and scalability; appropriate choices—representation-level objectives, multi-teacher signals, online protocols, and privacy-aware distillation—address these challenges and make KD a core tool for applied deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical toolkit to transfer performance and representational structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under memory, compute, or latency constraints. Research has expanded KD beyond simple soft-label matching to encompass intermediate-feature imitation, many-to-many layer mapping, relational and task-aware transfers, multi-teacher fusion, and input-side interventions (e.g., data augmentation or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students frequently approach teacher performance when methods are matched to the task and architecture, but significant open problems remain around robustness, low-frequency behavior, teacher errors, and data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Methods include soft-target or logit matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher and ensemble-driven transfer, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Distillation works both as a mechanism for transmitting ‘‘dark knowledge’’ about class relationships and as a regularizer that can improve student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, data or synthetic inputs, teacher design, and alignment between teacher and student. Practical goals—reducing inference cost, enabling edge deployment, preserving accuracy under domain shift, and meeting privacy or fairness constraints—are achievable in many settings but require task- and data-aware design. Open problems include robust, privacy-preserving distillation without teacher data, principled teacher selection and weighting, theoretical understanding of optimization gaps, and balancing compression with fairness and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Contextual Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of methods for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations and attention, and they can be combined with data strategies, multi-teacher schedules, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables real-world deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on principled choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate optimization and robustness limits. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a configurable, task-aware system rather than a single recipe, and it provides practical recommendations for designing effective distillation pipelines in NLP and related deep-learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Responses
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural signals. Across vision and NLP, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi- and self-teaching, and combinations with pruning/quantization—enable reduced inference cost and on-device deployment while attempting to retain performance. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD acts both as a route to transfer representational inductive biases and as a form of learned regularization; its success depends on signal choice, data provenance, capacity mismatch, and optimization. Methodological refinements (data augmentation, adversarial or boundary-focused examples, data-free synthesis, teacher design, and divergence choices) address core challenges in practice, but open problems remain around robustness, privacy, fairness, and reliably closing the teacher–student performance gap.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.
