papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression — Claims, Mechanisms, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—soft-output transfer, intermediate-representation alignment, and relational objectives—and is most powerful when composed with complementary techniques such as architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data-centric strategies. While KD frequently preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can enable real-world deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints, it is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, teacher errors, and rare-token or safety-critical behaviors create failure modes that require methodical mitigation. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core element of a wider compression pipeline, adopt task- and data-aware choices about what to transfer, and evaluate students on distributional, robustness, and application-specific criteria.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Across vision, language, retrieval, and graph domains, KD is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—enables substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical application requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained environments. KD encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and structural or layer-wise mappings. Its practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and protocols to teacher and student architectures, the availability and nature of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD can preserve much of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, degraded robustness under domain shift, and optimization challenges that require task-aware design and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible engineering paradigm for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what teacher signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data- or curriculum-driven strategies to use—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's task performance. Effective deployment requires pairing distillation with complementary compression methods, pretraining or adaptation of compact architectures, and explicit attention to limits such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, flexible strategy for compressing and adapting deep models for real-world deployment. When framed as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, teacher ensembles, data-aware synthesis, and architecture-aware compression—KD routinely yields compact students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to address robustness and rare-event behavior; when these are handled explicitly, KD enables reliable, deployable models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, multimodal, and language tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention supervision—are combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, synthetic, or public unlabeled) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on choosing appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student architectures and capacities, and handling limited or mismatched data; remaining challenges include optimization difficulty, propagation of teacher errors, and robust transfer of properties such as adversarial resistance or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system-level toolkit—combining logit matching, representation alignment, ensemble or multi-teacher signals, data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), and complementary compression techniques—KD frequently preserves much of a teacher’s performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and attention to robustness and bias transfer. Practical deployment therefore requires matching the distillation recipe to task requirements, student capacity, and data realities.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It is a flexible toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, and to support privacy- and data-constrained settings. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to the student capacity and task, choosing appropriate data or synthetic surrogates when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Key open problems include capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and principled design of teacher–student schedules.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-, latency-, or privacy-constrained environments. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while providing additional benefits such as implicit regularization, improved robustness in some settings, domain adaptation, and enabling training when original data are unavailable. A practical KD pipeline selects what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how to supply data (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free), and how to align teacher and student architectures; combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) typically yields the best trade-offs. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and distributional shift, optimization stability, preservation of low-frequency behaviors in NLP, and privacy constraints, which motivate hybrid, task-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep-learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation—regularly yield large runtime, memory, and latency gains when paired with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to prepare distillation data. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on student capacity, data availability, modality alignment, and complementary compression steps. I argue that KD should be treated as a configurable, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe, and I give practical design principles for when and how to apply it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolbox: Principles, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation should be understood and applied as a flexible set of techniques that go well beyond simple parameter compression. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, internal representation matching, layer-aware alignment, attention-guided mapping, and complementary compression methods—distillation can produce compact models that preserve accuracy, improve interpretability, and transfer robustness or privacy properties. Success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare the student, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher defects; practitioners benefit from system-level designs that pair distillation objectives with pre-training, data augmentation, and architecture-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies condense large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision students suitable for deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has produced a taxonomy of approaches—soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate/feature imitation, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher fusion, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling substantial gains in inference speed and memory; theoretical analyses attribute much of KD’s benefit to regularization from soft targets and the transfer of inductive biases. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors, operating without original training data, and designing adaptive, task-aware distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but it is not a single recipe: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, how distillation data are chosen or synthesized, and how complementary compression techniques are applied. Treating KD as a configurable system—combining appropriate loss forms, layer mappings, data strategies, and robustness/privacy safeguards—yields the best trade-offs between compactness and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Centrality, Mechanisms, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of a broader compression pipeline—combining choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—KD can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, its effectiveness is conditional: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, capacity limits, and risks of propagating teacher errors or biases require task-aware recipes and complementary techniques to produce reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models for deployment. KD operates by transferring useful behavior from a trained teacher to a compact student and can work through matching outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble signals. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), careful teacher–student alignment, and data strategies that address limited or private training data. KD yields strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) but has failure modes tied to student capacity, data mismatch, and propagation of teacher biases; production use therefore requires design-sensitive recipes and monitoring for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD enables practical trade-offs among accuracy, latency, privacy, and data availability by varying what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps), how it is transferred (layer-wise, channel-wise, adversarial), and which complementary compression strategies are applied (pruning, architecture search, quantization). When combined with techniques for limited or absent access to original training data, KD supports few-shot, zero-shot, and privacy-respecting workflows that make deployment feasible across modalities and resource constraints. Successful application requires selecting appropriate distilled signals and curricula, and often integrating KD with task- and architecture-specific methods.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Practical use of KD involves choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to handle data mismatches (data augmentation, synthetic data, or data-free methods), and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, federated protocols). Despite broad empirical success, open problems remain in preserving low-frequency behaviors, robustness and fairness, and in designing principled curricula and teacher-student interfaces for diverse deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques condense information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable ones. Across vision, speech, recommendation, generative models, and natural language processing, practitioners use a mix of logit-based soft-label supervision, feature imitation, data distillation, multi-teacher fusion, curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware search to trade accuracy for latency, memory, or interpretability. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher accuracy while enabling deployment in latency- or resource-constrained settings; theoretical and empirical analyses attribute much of KD’s effectiveness to the regularizing properties of soft targets, while recent extensions explicitly address adversarial robustness, decision-boundary transfer, domain adaptation, continual learning, and task-specific constraints. Remaining challenges include preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors (e.g., low-frequency phenomena), designing teacher-free or data-free alternatives, and building principled curricula and multi-source transfers that maximize student utility in downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original logit-based teacher-student paradigm to include feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, multi-teacher and adaptive-teacher strategies, and task- or hardware-aware compression. These methods have been applied across modalities — including vision, graphs, generative models, and a broad set of NLP tasks — and are increasingly combined with architecture search and pruning to meet deployment constraints. Despite empirical successes, important questions remain about what knowledge is most useful to transfer, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to operate under data, compute, or privacy limitations.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are widely used to transfer predictive behavior and representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. A broad family of methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher fusion, online and teacher-free protocols, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis—has been developed and evaluated across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Empirical studies show that, when designed carefully (teacher selection, data strategy, and objective choice), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling practical deployment; however, limitations remain around domain shift, robustness, preservation of fine-grained behaviors, and data- or architecture-mismatch, motivating hybrid strategies that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware training.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing models to smaller, efficient models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has diversified beyond simple teacher→student logit-matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, online and federated protocols, teacher-free and data-free variants, and architectural co-design. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D perception, and NLP demonstrates that carefully chosen distillation signals, layer mappings, and training practices (e.g., pretraining, projected feature matching, selective sample weighting) produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance; remaining challenges include data heterogeneity, privacy, robustness, and automating teacher–student pairing and signal selection.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Compression with Complementary Needs and Clear Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful engineering toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. In practice KD often delivers large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, but its success depends on task- and data-aware design: what signals are transferred, how teacher and student architectures are aligned, and how data scarcity, domain shift, privacy, and fairness concerns are handled. I argue KD should be the default starting point for compression pipelines, applied with explicit attention to complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware mapping), data strategies (data-free approaches or targeted synthesis), and safeguards against capacity mismatch and propagated biases.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practices, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Across vision and natural language processing, KD has become a flexible toolkit—combining logits/soft-targets, feature- or layer-level matching, data-side strategies (augmented or synthetic data), and architecture-aware student design—to produce compact models that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. Empirical work demonstrates meaningful efficiency gains in settings ranging from BERT compression to non-autoregressive translation, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary compression (architecture search, pruning, quantization) and from addressing optimization, privacy, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been widely adopted to reduce model size and runtime while retaining performance. Work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows multiple complementary strategies—logit matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and self-distillation—can be effective alone or in combination. Practical success depends on choices about teacher strength, student architecture, pre-training, and optimization, and recent systems integrate distillation with pruning, low-precision, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) unifies a set of techniques that transfer information from large, accurate teacher networks into smaller, faster student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Methods vary from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure, and are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign. Practical success depends on choices about the distillation signal, teacher–student alignment, availability and generation of training data, and optimization schedules. Across vision and language tasks, task-aware and deployment-aware distillation pipelines—often hybridizing multiple signals and synthesis or augmentation of data—produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though open problems remain around sample efficiency, robustness, fairness, and principled objective design.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool Beyond Simple Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be understood and applied as a flexible toolbox rather than merely a compression trick. KD enables compression, regularization, privacy-preserving transfer, and adaptation across diverse constraints (data scarcity, heterogeneous devices, federated settings). Effective practice combines soft-target supervision with representation-level alignment, architecture-aware methods (pruning, quantization, search), and privacy-aware or teacher-free variants. However, careful design is required to avoid capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness or bias degradation.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for producing compact models from large teachers that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention mimicry, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free synthesis—that routinely yield substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD has practical limits (data and domain mismatch, student capacity gaps, and safety/robustness concerns) that make it most effective when combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search, and robustness-aware objectives. Practitioners should treat KD as the core of a broader compression toolkit and adapt which knowledge is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and what auxiliary procedures (data augmentation, adversarial training, teacher design) are required to meet specific deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students. A rich family of KD methods—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, data-free and data-augmented distillation, and teacher-student co-design—has been developed to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) across vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation objectives, data strategies, and architecture choices are well matched. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, scarcity or absence of real data, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models. Practical pipelines combine pretraining of compact architectures, multi-objective distillation (outputs + internals), data augmentation or synthesis, and teacher adaptation to produce robust, efficient student models.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for transferring information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. KD techniques span output-level supervision (soft logits), intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, self- and progressive distillation, and data-free or zero-shot variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, speech, translation, detection, and generation) while enabling on-device and real-time use; success depends on the choice of distillation targets, the match between teacher and student capacity, the availability and quality of data, and appropriate regularization or augmentation during training. Practical deployment typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and privacy-aware mechanisms to produce robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Directions for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress large models into lightweight students for deployment. Recent work shows that KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size or computational cost, but gains depend on what knowledge is transferred, how teachers and students are prepared, and the distillation protocol. I argue that (1) transferring richer information than final logits, (2) preparing students with pre-training, (3) augmenting or synthesizing data during distillation, and (4) co-optimizing architecture-aware compression with distillation together form a robust recipe for reliable compression in NLP and other domains. These directions address generalization, data scarcity, and architectural differences, and they are supported by recent empirical and methodological studies across speech, vision, retrieval, and language modeling.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible tool for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and optimization difficulties—that require task-aware design choices around what to transfer, which teacher(s) to use, and how to prepare distillation data. A pragmatic pipeline that pre-trains compact models, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively combines KD with other compression steps yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression (and When to Combine It)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact deep and NLP models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD delivers consistent accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across modalities, improves small-model representations, and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not always sufficient on its own: success requires careful choice of transfer signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity and architecture, and integration with complementary compression, data, or training procedures to preserve rare or safety-critical behaviors. I argue that KD should be treated as the central element of a compression toolkit, applied pragmatically with domain- and deployment-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Practical Priorities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students that are suitable for real-world deployment. When treated as a flexible toolkit and combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, KD reliably reduces memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, data limitations, domain shift, and rare-token or safety-critical behaviors require careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, System-Level Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed as a flexible, system-level toolbox that transfers predictive behavior and intermediate structure from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free procedures), KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving most of the teacher’s utility. However, its success is conditional: practitioner choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, and data regime materially affect outcomes; KD is not a universal fix for robustness, domain shift, or bias propagation. I argue that KD should be applied as an integrated engineering practice with clear evaluation of limits and targeted remedies for the known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool to make large deep models practical: it reduces model size and latency, enables domain adaptation, preserves privacy and scalability, and can even improve robustness when applied carefully. Successful deployments balance which teacher signals are transferred (logits, features, attention or answers), how they are aligned (layer-wise, projector-mediated, task-aware filters), and the training setup (multi-teacher, online, or adversarial). I argue that a principled combination of feature-level guidance, task-aware selection, and appropriate distillation architecture gives the best tradeoffs for NLP deployment: it preserves downstream performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude gains in speed, capacity, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Practical Knowledge Distillation for Deploying Large NLP and Deep Models: A Unified Argument for Multi-Teacher, Data-Agnostic, and Federated Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and essential set of techniques for compressing large deep and language models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. A mature KD strategy must simultaneously preserve teacher knowledge, generalize across domains and distributions, and respect deployment constraints (e.g., lack of original data or heterogeneous client devices). Empirical and methodological advances show that combining multi-teacher strategies, data-agnostic/distillation-from-generator approaches, feature-level projectors or ensembles, targeted augmentation, and adaptations for federated settings yields robust, efficient student models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It is a flexible toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, and to support privacy- and data-constrained settings. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to the student capacity and task, choosing appropriate data or synthetic surrogates when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Key open problems include capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and principled design of teacher–student schedules.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power and internal knowledge from large, expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students), enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, designing many-to-many layer mappings, performing data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable, and distilling ensembles or multiple teachers into a single model. In NLP, these methods are applied to compress pre-trained language models, speed up evaluation metrics, and produce task-adaptive compressed models while attempting to retain generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates many strategies for transferring information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. The field encompasses matching teacher outputs (soft logits), imitating intermediate representations, transferring structural or relational knowledge, and combining distillation with architecture changes, data augmentation, or privacy- and communication-aware protocols. Across computer vision, generation, recommendation, and many NLP tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameters and latency while often preserving most of the original performance; success depends on which knowledge is transferred, how architectures are aligned, data availability, and capacity/robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single training trick but a central, practical framework for compressing large models into deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-label transfer, representation-level alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and integration with other compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate design: choosing which teacher signals to transfer, addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, and using data-aware or data-free strategies when original training data are unavailable. I argue that KD should be the core component of any production-focused compression pipeline, paired with representation-level objectives and careful data strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Complementary Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations across many tasks and modalities, enabling substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not sufficient by itself in all settings: its success depends on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases or errors. For robust, deployable compression, KD should be treated as the central element of a broader pipeline that includes data synthesis or augmentation, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or progressive module replacement), plus careful attention to privacy, fairness, and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, system-level toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques transfer information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure; they can be combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies that include augmentation, synthetic generation, or data-free approaches. Effective distillation depends on matching the distillation signals, student architecture, and data strategy to task and deployment constraints. While well-designed KD pipelines often recover most teacher performance, remaining challenges include optimization instability, transfer of teacher errors or biases, handling limited or private data, and preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: The Central, Practical, and Conditional Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of techniques for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. KD methods span soft-target matching, intermediate representation and layer-wise alignment, ensemble-to-single transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-conscious pipelines. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that approach teacher performance across NLP, speech, and vision tasks, and that combining KD with architecture-aware compression or augmentation strategies often yields the best trade-offs. However, KD has limits: student capacity, the availability and quality of distilled data, and inherited teacher biases can all constrain outcomes. Responsible and effective compression therefore requires selecting the appropriate distillation signals, considering task and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or fairness-aware objectives).

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression, Regularization, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a flexible, multi-purpose methodology rather than only a compression trick. KD enables smaller, efficient models for deployment, but it also serves as a mechanism for learned regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release. Practical success relies on matching the distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), the teacher selection and scheduling, and the data or data-generation strategy to the deployment constraints. Combining logits-based supervision with representation-level objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware query mechanisms produces more reliable and robust student models for real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. KD encompasses multiple information channels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and is commonly used together with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data (real, augmented, or synthesized). While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can serve additional roles such as regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release, it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain shift, and propagation of teacher errors—that necessitate careful pipeline design and complementary methods for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central tool for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers to smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a system—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—it delivers large practical wins in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving most task performance. Responsible use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.
