papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression methods form a versatile toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Work in the past decade has expanded simple teacher→student logit matching into a broad set of techniques that match intermediate representations, exploit attention or structural signals, operate with or without access to original training data, and combine with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher quality across language, vision, and retrieval tasks when distillation objectives, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen deliberately. Important practical concerns remain: optimization and capacity mismatches that limit perfect teacher replication, distributional or privacy constraints on distillation data, and trade-offs between fidelity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques form a flexible set of training paradigms that transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large 'teacher' networks into smaller, faster 'student' models. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, practitioners use logit/soft-target matching, intermediate feature or attention alignment, relational objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free procedures to shrink models while retaining much of their utility. Effective distillation typically combines careful selection of distillation targets, student preparation (architecture choice or pretraining), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). While distilled students often approach teacher performance in many settings, remaining challenges include capacity and optimization gaps, domain- or data-shift, preservation of rare-token behavior and fairness, and principled design for data-free or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. It is used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, to protect privacy, and to adapt models across domains. Practical distillation methods vary in what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers are chosen (single, multi-teacher, self), and how training is regularized (data augmentation, loss design, adversarial objectives). While distillation often yields students that outperform similarly sized models trained from scratch, mismatches between teacher and student, optimization difficulties, and domain/privacy constraints remain important concerns. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and language tasks shows that careful design choices (data augmentation, multi-stage distillation, private/noisy queries, and specialized losses) meaningfully affect student performance and deployment trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing smaller, faster models from large pretrained teachers. KD operates through multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and yields substantial efficiency gains when paired with complementary methods and task-aware design. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, or optimal hardware utilization: achieving production-grade compression requires matching distillation objectives to data availability, architecture mismatch, privacy constraints, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the core of a multi-tool compression pipeline—central to practical deployment but reliant on deliberate system-level choices to realize its benefits reliably.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, system-level toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques transfer information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure; they can be combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies that include augmentation, synthetic generation, or data-free approaches. Effective distillation depends on matching the distillation signals, student architecture, and data strategy to task and deployment constraints. While well-designed KD pipelines often recover most teacher performance, remaining challenges include optimization instability, transfer of teacher errors or biases, handling limited or private data, and preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and versatile tool available today for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and privacy-preserving mechanisms), KD enables production-ready models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization instability, and risks of propagating teacher errors demand task-aware design, careful data handling, and hybrid engineering practices to obtain reliable results in realistic deployments.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, mature toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Approaches vary from transferring softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, from online and multi-teacher schemes to data-free and privacy-aware pipelines. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and other modalities shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while delivering substantial reductions in inference cost, parameter count, and memory footprint. Practical success depends on matching distillation targets and schedules to student capacity and deployment constraints, handling limited or private data appropriately, and addressing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students by transferring learned behavior or representations. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational information and are often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on what signals are transferred, student capacity and initialization, data strategies during distillation, and addressing robustness, privacy, and distributional mismatch. While distilled students frequently approach teacher performance, open problems remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preventing transfer of teacher errors or biases, and designing data-efficient or privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a configurable system rather than a single recipe. By choosing which teacher signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, and applying task- and data-aware strategies (including multi-teacher aggregation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and architecture search), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD delivers practical gains across vision and NLP but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors, mismatching capacities, or degrading robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relations. A diverse set of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data augmentation or synthesis, and deployment-aware co-design with pruning/quantization—are combined in practice to meet latency, memory, privacy, and communication constraints. While distilled students often recover most of teachers' accuracy, success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods; outstanding challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving long-tail behaviors, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD encompasses transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure; it can be combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, parameter sharing) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic generation, data‑free rehearsal) to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatches, data or domain shift, and risk of propagating teacher errors require task‑aware design, complementary compression methods, and careful validation. When applied as a principled toolkit — choosing what to transfer, how to align representations, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to integrate pruning/quantization — KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). Across vision and language, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architectural design, and quantization) and with strategies for scarce or missing data to obtain deployable models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and mechanisms to preserve robustness and rare-token behaviors. Data-free distillation, multi-task or multi-teacher schemes, and targeted representation matching extend KD’s applicability to many real-world settings.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, selective sample transfer, multi-teacher and data-free strategies—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, managing data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and addressing harms such as transferred biases or degraded rare-token behavior. A pragmatic pipeline mixes pretraining, representation-aware losses, targeted data manipulations, and teacher-aware design to achieve favorable trade-offs among efficiency, accuracy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, graph learning, and distributed settings, KD variants—soft-target matching, representation- and relational-level supervision, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or federated protocols—have enabled substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical gains depend on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited, private, or heterogeneous data; consequently KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates many strategies for transferring information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. The field encompasses matching teacher outputs (soft logits), imitating intermediate representations, transferring structural or relational knowledge, and combining distillation with architecture changes, data augmentation, or privacy- and communication-aware protocols. Across computer vision, generation, recommendation, and many NLP tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameters and latency while often preserving most of the original performance; success depends on which knowledge is transferred, how architectures are aligned, data availability, and capacity/robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavioral or representational information from a teacher to a student. Across computer vision and NLP, distillation methods vary from matching output soft targets to aligning internal representations, performing self-distillation, and synthesizing or selecting data when original training examples are unavailable. Empirical work shows distillation can retain much of teacher performance while enabling domain adaptation, improved generalization, and deployment under latency or memory constraints. However, effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, layers, features), the availability and complexity of training data, regularization (e.g., label smoothing and augmentation), and fairness or privacy constraints. Open challenges include understanding when students can outperform teachers, balancing bias mitigation and utility, and combining distillation with pruning or hardware-aware compression for edge deployment.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. The technique has diversified into a family of methods (logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free and federated variants) and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and augmentation to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on matching distillation strategy to goals (latency, privacy, robustness) and on careful handling of teacher quality, student capacity, and available data.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured relational signals—and is effective across modalities when paired with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and student-aware architecture design. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, selecting appropriate distillation targets, preparing or synthesizing suitable training data, and validating robustness and fairness. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a system of interacting components (signal selection, data, initialization, and optimization) and couples distillation with architecture-aware transforms, pruning, or quantization to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across tasks and modalities. KD's benefits arise from multiple mechanisms: transferring soft output distributions, mimicking intermediate features, providing regularization that improves generalization, and enabling compression even when original training data are unavailable. Empirically and theoretically, KD should be treated as a toolbox: select loss forms (logit, feature, relational), augment or synthesize data when needed, and consider joint training of teacher and student or teacher design that is friendly to students. Combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture design), KD helps produce efficient models that retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD is effective across modalities and tasks, from question answering and speech recognition to vision and federated learning, but its success depends on careful handling of teacher imperfections, data artifacts, and deployment constraints. Best practices include using multi-teacher or staged distillation, blending soft and hard targets, engineering teacher-student interfaces (e.g., projectors or student-aware teachers), and combining KD with complementary techniques such as quantization or federated momentum. When these strategies are applied thoughtfully, KD enables high-quality compact models suitable for real-world, resource-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Best Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a comprehensive, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision and natural language tasks. When designed as a system—selecting appropriate teacher signals, leveraging intermediate representations, using data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, distillation has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, propagation of teacher errors) and open research needs (reliable data-free methods, robustness and fairness preservation, principled teacher selection). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central engineering primitive for practical model compression, and it outlines evidence-based best practices and remaining research priorities to make distillation robust for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of the teacher’s predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of methods—matching output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, data availability, privacy, and multimodal inputs. Empirical work shows that when the distillation recipe is matched to model architectures, data conditions, and deployment constraints, students can retain much of the teacher’s performance while offering practical efficiency gains; however, trade-offs and open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Practical Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core set of techniques for converting large, expensive neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for real-world deployment. KD variants transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural behaviors; they can be combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture modification) and adapted for constrained data, privacy, and deployment regimes. However, distillation’s success depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate teacher-induced errors or biases. Practical deployments therefore require task-aware distillation design, careful teacher selection or adaptation, and evaluation of failure modes such as degraded rare-token behavior or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search or data augmentation—enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical successes span classification, object detection, machine translation, and language-model compression, but practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to curate or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. The method’s effectiveness arises partly from the regularizing properties of soft targets and richer teacher signals, yet distillation can propagate teacher errors and struggle with capacity, data heterogeneity, and robustness unless augmented by task-aware design or additional engineering.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses information from large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The approach has diversified from soft-label matching into a toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or combinations thereof; it can be adapted to settings with limited or no access to original training data, and it is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and integrating KD into a broader compression pipeline that validates robustness and fairness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Washington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood and used not as a single recipe but as a flexible, multi-component toolkit for producing compact models that meet real-world deployment constraints. When designers choose what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), align teacher and student architectures thoughtfully, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, KD reliably produces students that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory use, and deployment complexity. Practical success requires attention to capacity mismatch, task-specific selection of signals, and safeguards for robustness and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models for deployment. KD operates by transferring useful behavior from a trained teacher to a compact student and can work through matching outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble signals. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), careful teacher–student alignment, and data strategies that address limited or private training data. KD yields strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) but has failure modes tied to student capacity, data mismatch, and propagation of teacher biases; production use therefore requires design-sensitive recipes and monitoring for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. When treated as a system—deciding what signals to transfer (soft outputs, internal representations, relations), how to prepare or synthesize data, how to design teachers and students, and how to combine KD with complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization—KD enables deployable models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on capacity matching, data availability, and task-aware objectives; addressing robustness, fairness, and privacy requires targeted interventions and monitoring.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical, Private, and Robust Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often framed narrowly as a model-compression trick to shrink large neural networks. This paper argues KD should instead be viewed as a core engineering and scientific tool for practical deployment: it enables training with limited or private data, yields task- and domain-adaptive compact models, improves robustness and fairness, and transfers intermediate representations and attention patterns that standard supervised training cannot. We synthesize evidence from recent work to show how variants of KD—self-distillation, layer-wise projection, multi-teacher schemes, teacher annealing, and data-free distillation—address concrete deployment challenges in vision and NLP, and we derive practical recommendations for combining these techniques in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students) so the students retain much of the teacher utility while fitting deployment constraints. Research has produced a variety of distillation paradigms: logit- and soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise and channel-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, self-supervised distillation, multi-teacher ensembles and domain-aware adaptation. Empirical work shows that combining pre-training for compact architectures with distillation, using task-aware selection of teacher signals, and tailoring distillation to modality- or task-specific structure leads to stronger compressed models. Important open issues include distillation without access to original data, preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models, and closing the capacity gap between teacher and student without over-constraining the student.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: when treated as a broad training paradigm it enables compact, robust, and deployable models across modalities and tasks. By integrating logit-level guidance, intermediate feature transfer, architecture-aware projectors, adaptive teacher selection, data- and domain-aware strategies, and robustness-aware objectives, KD pipelines can produce students that approach teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success requires designing what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous components, and how to shape inputs and curricula for the student—rather than relying on a single generic distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central Tool That Must Be Used as a Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a vital method for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, speech, and NLP shows that matching teacher outputs and internal signals can yield students that recover much of teacher accuracy while delivering large gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, KD is not a single recipe: practical success depends on which teacher signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, what data are used (real, augmented, or synthetic), and whether distillation is combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Careful, task-aware design and hybrid pipelines are therefore required to realize robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Best Practices and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable models across vision, language, and structured-data domains. KD works at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention, and structural guidance) and combines naturally with complementary methods—student pretraining, data augmentation or synthesis, multi-teacher and ensemble signals, architecture-aware losses, and privacy-aware generation—to produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s utility while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective deployment requires careful choices of distillation targets, alignment strategies, and data-handling procedures, and awareness of common failure modes (optimization instability, teacher error propagation, and domain/device heterogeneity).

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The practice spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, and using multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Effective distillation depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to manage robustness and privacy concerns. While KD often preserves much of a teacher's utility in deployed models, limits remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, rare-token behavior, and principled teacher selection, motivating integrated, multi-level distillation pipelines and further empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior and representations from a teacher to a student. Methods span matching teacher output distributions (soft labels), aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, adversarial or data-free approaches, and online or federated variants that trade communication and privacy constraints against fidelity. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage imperfect or heterogeneous data and devices, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression strategies (e.g., pruning or architecture search). While distilled students often retain much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency or resource constraints, open challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, handling domain shift and robustness, and designing privacy- and communication-efficient protocols for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task‑Aware, Integrated Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical engine for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and adapted to task constraints—what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data limitations—KD routinely yields strong tradeoffs between efficiency and performance. However, its benefits are conditional: student capacity, data heterogeneity, teacher artifacts, and robustness or privacy constraints limit outcomes unless KD is combined with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data synthesis) and applied with deliberate, task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Pre-training Plus Strategic Distillation: Practical Principles for Compressing Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when combined with deliberate choices about pre-training, the form of knowledge transferred, data manipulation during distillation, and adaptive teacher-student dynamics. Compact models that are pre-trained, trained to mimic both outputs and internal representations, and exposed to carefully designed augmented or mixed inputs can match much of the performance of larger models while meeting deployment constraints. However, compression success depends critically on optimization, data distribution, and task-specific phenomena such as rare-word behavior in sequence generation. I argue that a pragmatic pipeline—pre-train compact architectures, distill soft targets and internal representations, use augmentation/mixing to shape training data complexity, and apply adaptive or meta-learned teacher strategies—offers the best trade-off between efficiency and accuracy for deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, modular technique in modern model-compression pipelines: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller students while remaining flexible enough to combine with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-side interventions. KD’s practical success depends on deliberate choices—what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to evaluate robustness and long-tail behavior. When used as part of a system that addresses optimization, data, and mismatch issues, KD frequently yields compact models that meet deployment constraints; when used alone or carelessly it can underperform or propagate undesirable behaviors. The remainder of this paper argues for KD as the default, central component of compression toolkits while outlining its limits and concrete design recommendations to mitigate them.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It can transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, structured relational signals, or ensemble knowledge, and supports data-side strategies including data-free and augmentation-aware schemes. In practice, KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance when its formulation is matched to task constraints, data availability, and student capacity. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or privacy-preserving compression: practitioner success hinges on selecting appropriate distillation signals, addressing teacher–student and data mismatches, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practical Patterns, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relational signals. A broad set of techniques—soft-target matching, representation- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, self- or data-free distillation, and integration with pruning/quantization or architecture adaptation—enables large reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate data; predictable failure modes include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and transfer of teacher errors or biases. Practical deployment treats KD as an engineering toolkit that must be adapted to task, data, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while often preserving — and in some settings improving — task performance. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, and they are frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture transformation) and with data-aware strategies (multi-stage distillation, multi-teacher schedules, or data synthesis) to meet deployment constraints. KD’s benefits arise both from transferring predictive behavior and from inducing useful regularization, but practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, the provenance or synthesis of distillation data, and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression approaches transform large, high-performance neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to matching intermediate representations, designing task-aware layer mappings, synthesizing or augmenting data for training, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications include compressing pretrained transformers for NLP, improving robustness under domain shift, enabling on-device inference and federated learning with heterogeneous devices, and training non-autoregressive sequence models. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and limitations: distillation can yield compact models with strong accuracy but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability or synthesis of data, and handling low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Deployment-First System: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modality-agnostic technique for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, selection of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is conditional on choices of what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or structural behavior), student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and task-aware training procedures. Effective compression therefore requires distillation objectives and pipelines matched to the deployment constraints and to the nature of the teacher and task.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Practical Centrality and Conditional Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core engineering and research tool to compress large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical results across tasks and modalities show KD can substantially reduce parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, and KD integrates naturally with complementary techniques (low-precision numerics, architecture search, pruning, federated or privacy-aware pipelines). At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and robustness concerns require careful design choices and hybrid strategies. Effective deployment therefore depends on selecting which knowledge to transfer, adapting distillation signals to data and architecture mismatches, and combining KD with targeted algorithmic and system-level adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Pipeline Design, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most usefully viewed as a system-level, modular pipeline for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When KD combines soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, selective or synthesized data, multi-teacher aggregation, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery), it reliably yields small students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of transferred biases and domain shifts. Practical deployments therefore require principled choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and which data strategies to apply.
